items.body: Those of us who have been digging into Analog Africa�s increasingly formidable releases over the last two decades are well aware of the massive amount of raw, vodun-based Sato and Sakpata-derived funk the label has issued by Benin�s most prolific 1970s-era band, the Orchestre Poly-Ritmo. AA has dropped no fewer than 3 compilations of their heaviest material, as well as a reissue of the band�s first LP, in an effort to give them the international status they deserve. That being said, what might be different about this collection of their music? And who is Antoine Dougb�? Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa As it turns out, Dougb� was a song-conjurer whose mode of musical transfer was slapping his legs in a rhythm known as Cavacha, a groove created by drummer Belobi Meridjo, who was inspired by a train cadence that he worked into a pattern that ultimately spread like a 21st century California wildfire throughout Congolese pop music in the mid-1970s. Dougb�, known as the �Devil�s Prime Minister,� was also a practitioner of vodun who inspired fear in any musician he felt was unsuited to play his music, which is how he landed on working exclusively Poly-Ritmo, as he felt they could nail what he wanted in ways other bands couldn�t. His recording career was brief - 3 albums and a few singles - but as this collection shows, it was potent. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa Because of the era from which this music dates, it�s not surprising that the recording and instrument tones have changed - the guitars have a plastic sheen and synthesizers appear- even if the music remains rooted in the 1970s. Perhaps the influence of the Cuban son is more apparent here than on other Poly-Ritmo collections, especially in the collection�s initial offerings. And yes, Congolese rumba, then shaking all of sub-Saharan Africa to its knees, is present too. �Ma Won Min Towe Leo� is one example. Opening with a bed of synthesizers, the shimmering guitars, tinny, seemingly squeezed dry by the 80s themselves, lock in over relentless high-hat-focused grooves. The guitars finally start firing in different directions midway through, before that synth weaves back in, forming a bed underneath it all. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa �We Tayi Sin Assi Tche� is much more overtly Cuban. With its insistent cowbell, classic, nasal vocal call and response, and tight, repeated guitar figures, its debt to mid-twentieth century Afro-Cuban sons is transparent. Another track, �Djomido Ma Dougbe Tche� rides a groove reminiscent of 70�s-era Franco classic �Liberte.� The pulse is relentless, and the guitar solo repeats a tight repetition of a few notes, driving listeners to ecstasy all the while. However, none of this music is a mere copy of its influences; rather, like so much potent pop coming from the continent at the time, it is a swirl of major influences rendered by local rhythms and vocal phrasing to give it specific identity, in this case, to Benin. Dougb�s musical role on this collection is a bit murky. One of his three albums has a photo of him, fully mic�d behind a collection of hand drums, so perhaps he served as a percussionist/vocalist; this release never explains. He wasn�t a songwriter in the traditional sense. It seems he was more of an instigator and arranger, but his thumbprint was apparently heavy enough to warrant his name on the records he was involved with. Whatever the case, in his brief run as a recording artist, he and Poly-Ritmo produced a handful of driving, Cavacha-inspired grooves that can still wear holes in club floors. Further reading: Petrona Mart�nez - Ancestras (Review) Gnonnas Pedro & His Dadjes - Roi De L'Agbadja Moderne 1974-1983 (Review)

items.body: Tako Toki are like desert island musicians who, castaway without their instruments, were forced to construct their own. Lucky for us, they are as skilled in making instruments as they are in creating original songs with which to show off their handicrafts. Un Dimanche � Monaco is the band�s follow-up to their well-received debut, Hirsute Farfelus , with a similar mash of musical styles. Before discussing the music, we need to talk about their instrument closet. They really have built everything they play out of bric-a-brac, odds and ends, and rubbish. I�m not sure from listening which is which, but they call their instruments, in an incomplete list, tassofons, tilofons, and tubofones, clarinuts, didjerimou, and klarbass, and my favorite, kitchenofon. (I will refer to what I hear by the names of store-bought instruments that they sound like.) The most surprising thing for me was how accurate the instruments were to pitch and how good they sounded under the harsh scrutiny of modern recording microphones that have documented a rich, high-quality sound. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki They have also very effectively matched their choice of instruments with the style of music that inspires their compositions. Right off the top, �Yinitza� features a laughing clarinet singing a klezmer tune accompanied by bassoon for the bass, frantic two-time percussion, and the exuberant human yelps found on many klezmer recordings. As on this track, many tunes feature improvisations that show an impressive degree of musicianship. On the cumbia-inspired �Le Cuenta,� the characteristic flute carries the tune, augmented by a Spanish singing chorus, and remarkably rich-sounding Latin percussion. The title track surrounds us with afrobeat woodblocks, shakers, and rattles scattered around the mix. The melody is played on a marimba ornamented with bells and cymbals. Again, the lead player improvises over the tune and often against the beat with jazzy chops. The flute returns on the samba-inspired �Ambiguidade,� and on �Aksum� it traces a trance-like Middle Eastern tune reminiscent of a 60s TV spy-show theme. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki Full of fun and one of a kind, Un Dimanche � Monaco celebrates our universal love of rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic sounds and the varied, wonderful ways cultures have organized that love in what we call music. At the same time, playing on literal pieces of junk, Tako Tiko reminds us, as we contemplate many mall music shops filled with gleaming wood and brass instruments and countless unused guitars lying in closets, that musicians will always find a way to make music. Find the artist online. Further reading: Tako Toki - Hirsute Farfelus (Review) Terje Isungset - Glacial Poetry (Review)

items._cn_summary: Tako Toki 乐队的这张专辑延续了首作《Hirsute Farfelus》的杂糅风格，但最引人注目的并非风格本身，而是他们的乐器：所有演奏设备均由零碎杂物和废旧物品自制而成，包括所谓 tassofons、kitchenofon、klarbass 等奇异造物。尽管材料简陋，这些自制乐器在现代录音麦克风的苛刻捕捉下竟呈现出准确的音高与丰富的音质。音乐层面，乐队将克莱兹默、昆比亚、桑巴、非洲节拍与中东旋律等多种世界音乐元素熔于一炉，旋律由各种自制管乐器与马林巴琴承担，即兴段落展现出扎实的演奏功底。配器选择与曲风高度契合，各曲风格虽多却保持了整体的趣味与连贯性。专辑最终传递出一种理念：音乐的本质在于节奏、旋律与和声的文化表达，而非乐器的材质。

items.body: After the extra-terrestial explorations of Eventyrferd , the previous album from Norway's Camilla Hole Trio, in which sci-fi synth sounds were married with traditional material, their latest release Langs is rather more earthbound. But the quest to look beyond their own country's folk music continues. Camilla Hole's main instrument being the soprano sax, the influence of jazz is unsurprising and this is evident in the opening track �Springleik,� signifying a tune used to accompany the springleik dance from the west of Norway. Initially Hole takes the melody with Egil Kalman and Knut Kvifte Nesheim providing rhythmic support on double bass and drums respectively, with the overdubbing of Kalman's modular synth and Nesheim's vibraphone adding colour. But characteristically for this trio, in which assigned roles are never clearly defined or adhered to, things soon start to move around, with Kalman taking up the melody on his bass, playing the melody in unison with Hole, while Nesheim opens things out further rhythmically. As the whole piece takes on a much more improvisatory feel, Hole plays the melody one more time as things draw to a close. Langs by Camilla Hole Trio
items.label: Taragot
items._cn_summary: 挪威Camilla Hole Trio在《Langs》中延续了对本土民间音乐素材的再探索，但相比前作偏向外太空科幻合成器音色的风格，本次回归更为脚踏实地。Hole以高音萨克斯为主导，与低音提琴和鼓构成核心三重奏架构，同时以模块合成器和颤音琴作为色彩叠加层。作品中乐手角色并不固定，三人在即兴框架中不断互换旋律与节奏职能：开篇曲目《Springleik》源自挪威西部传统舞曲，Kalman和Nesheim首先提供节奏支撑，随后Kalman以贝斯与Hole齐奏旋律，Nesheim扩展节奏维度，Hole在尾声再次出场完成收束。整体呈现出开放式的即兴对话，将传统民间曲调与现代爵士即兴手法融合探讨。

items.body: Kr�ta , the latest release on Norway's Taragot label, features a Swede and two Norwegians playing interpretations of mainly traditional tunes from their respective countries. Fiddler Mats Ed�n has long been involved in Swedish folk music, as a player, composer and teacher, and in the process exploring and integrating different musical styles and approaches. Tellef Kvifte was in the pioneering Norwegian crossover band Slinkombas in the 1970s and has continued to play a central role in Norwegian folk music, both as a musician and an academic. Most often heard playing the sj�fl�yte , more widely known as a recorder, Kvifte has employed other instruments from outside the Norwegian tradition, in particular the saxophone and bagpipes. His son Knut Kvifte Nesheim , a drummer and composer, has also shown a determination to blur the lines between different musical genres, both in his solo and group projects. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio It comes as no surprise then to find this trio offering a far from conventional take on the tunes they have chosen. While dance tunes may be the source of most of the material here, this feels more akin to chamber music; not that it is remotely classical in style, but in the sense it conveys of three players engrossed in a musically intimate conversation. This is not a performance appropriate for accompanying dancers but might instead be seen as an exploration of hidden possibilities of meaning in the music. In so doing it reveals some of its underlying mystery, including, perhaps, a darker side. Just as in an Ibsen play, where the surface bonhomie, jollity and social nicety can be hiding something more sinister, in Scandinavian dance music there are at times hints of a troublesome undercurrent below the surface. So the decision to open proceedings with �Fossgrimen,� a fiddle tune from Norway's Setesdal valley, is perhaps significant. A fossgrimen is a mythical creature, a kind of water-sprite living in waterfalls from whom fiddle-players were considered to have learned their skills and for that were not universally welcomed, with the fiddle considered to be the devil's instrument. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio Tellef Kvifte takes the lead melody on most tracks but on the Swedish �Polska from Per Myhr,� having played a repeated introductory riff on the sj�fl�yte, with Mats Ed�n providing an amorphous textural accompaniment below and Nesheim adding some quiet tinkling, it's Ed�n who introduces the tune on the fiddle with Kvifte proceeding to play in unison. It's a short track and almost as soon as it gets going things start to fragment and everything grind to a halt.
items.label: Taragot
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由瑞典小提琴家与两位挪威乐手组成的三重奏演绎，将斯堪的纳维亚传统舞曲素材置于室内乐式的亲密对话中重新审视。乐评指出，作品虽以传统旋律为出发点，却并非为舞蹈伴奏而作，而是三位演奏者对音乐深层含义的探索，揭示出表面欢愉之下的暗流。评论以挪威Setesdal地区的"Fossgrimen"传说开篇，将小提琴与水妖、魔鬼乐器等北欧民间意象相连，暗示专辑对音乐神秘性的关注。在器乐配置上，竖笛、萨克斯、风笛与传统小提琴、鼓组并置，打破常规民乐器乐组合。三首曲目中，乐手通过模糊的纹理铺垫、齐奏与碎片化处理，让旋律在成形与瓦解之间游走，展现出对传统素材的实验性解构态度。

items.body: Sendas by Omar Sosa True to a Monk-inspired commitment never to play the same thing twice, Cuban pianist and composer Omar Sosa�s Sendas (Pathways), his latest solo offering, is the vivid invention of a pensive, restlessly creative, evolutionary artistry. As with all Sosa�s work, Sendas is the fortunate product of serendipity. In 2021 the COVID lockdown was underway, his marriage was ending, and a scheduled Milan appearance cancellation garnered an invitation to record at the Fazioli Pianoforti Concert Hall, annex to the renowned Italian piano manufactory in Sacile, Pordenone, about an hour northeast of Venice. At Fazioli, Sosa found himself in august company. Herbie Hancock and a host of classical pianists are Fazioli artists. Among the institutions that have embraced the Fazioli sound are the Juilliard School, Teatro La Fenice (Venice), the Budapest Palace of Arts, the Paris Conservatory, the Beijing Grand Theatre, and the universities of Salzburg, Graz, and Vienna. An unscripted two-hour solo improvisation on a Fazioli grand in the empty concert hall provided the raw audio for Sendas , later to be flavored in the mix, sparsely, with voice clips, percussion, loops, field recordings, found sounds effects that Sosa has collected over a career spanning four decades. As Sosa related to me soon after completing the post-production of Sendas , �Humanity is spiritually lost. We humans are all in this together. We need to evolve, but always keeping the traditions, walking with a strong, determined pace. We need more grounded music with overtones that resonate with the lower chakras� like throat singing, a mantra of the universal music.� �Creativity is about combining all your influences in a new way. I don�t aspire to be jazz, Latin, timba, reggaeton, classical. I avoid styles, but I respect the forms.� �I try not to think about how listeners will receive it but I do try to address their expectations, and go with the music to some other new place. Many free spirits come to listen, to be a part of the journey we are on.� Sosa laughs, �My son says, �Your niche is really small.� But the people who come really are there to be part of what we are going to do.� �Economics, technology, the streaming ear wash, algorithms all want to put you into a defined category � and so do many music journalists! The industry�s mentality is that any investment in artists must be defined by market categories to be profitable.� �But I play to be free of that,� Sosa says. �I play without thinking. There are no wrong notes. I love the first take. That�s the take, the natural voice of your soul. �Less is more� is a mantra in my life and music.� Consider the opening of �Inside the Spirit,� easing in leisurely, reaching over the keyboard into the resonant heart of the instrument, plucking and stroking the strings, teasing out a fuller resonance � only later to be embellished in the studio mix with light percussion and the muted Spanish-language refrain of a pregonero or street vendor, as might be heard in the calles of Havana or any other Latin American barrio. Sendas by Omar Sosa Moving from the secular to the sacred, �Deities Serenade� is an Afro-Cuban invocation of the shape-shifting divine, yet with ample room for ecumenical recasting in accord with a listener�s own self-location. �Inside My Soul� and �Something from Home� are Sosa works that to my ear may be an intuitive response to the distant call of Chopin�s "Nocturnes," to which Sosa says he listened every night for two years as a conservatory student in Cuba. Sendas by Omar Sosa �Caribbean Movement� and �Shirma� speak to Sosa�s rootedness in the lyrical, rhythmic, and harmonic heritage of the plantation islands where African and European cultures tragically entwined. In the violent forging of the world�s first truly modern people, social, cultural, linguistic, and musical displacements proved more flexible and accommodating than many of those same people, who shaped a contentious convergence of traditions into a changing same that persists into the unfolding present, ever yet to come. With expressive transcendence such as this, seeking to reduce the spiritual essence and inspiration of Sosa�s music to words is rather a fool�s errand. Better rather to listen, to contemplate, to perceive the pathway, to wander the sonic sendas coursing to the next way station without prejudice or preconception. To that end, Scott Price, Sosa�s longtime manager and friend relates, �We are using Sendas as the springboard for our first experiments in AI-generated Omar Sosa music videos.� Absent the opportunity to see and hear Sosa perform live, the palpable ideal, these ancillary audiovisual experiments further the ineffability of his artistic quest, the unique nature of the listening experience and all that ensues.

items._cn_summary: 古巴钢琴家Omar Sosa的专辑《Sendas》录制于意大利Fazioli钢琴音乐厅，基于一场两小时的无脚本独奏即兴，后期叠加人声采样、打击乐、循环段落、田野录音与环境音效。Sosa本人跨越四十年职业生涯，回避风格归类，融合爵士、拉美传统、古典与电子元素，强调即兴首遍的直觉性创作哲学。专辑探讨精神失落与人类共在的主题，通过冥想式的钢琴演奏呼应喉音唱诵与低脉轮共振的概念。评论对作品背景、制作过程与艺术家的创作观念有详细阐述，包含多段直接引语，但正文内容似乎在曲目分析处截断。整体呈现跨界即兴钢琴与世界音乐美学相结合的个人化声音探索。

items.body: After nine previous albums and a 25-year career at the forefront of world music, Lucas Santtana is fluent in the many genres of Brazilian music. His new project, Brasiliano , is a musical exploration of the languages of Brazil. With songs sung in Portuguese, French, English, Spanish, Occitan, Cape Verde Creole, and Tupy-Guarani, a Brazilian native language, Santtana has assembled guest lyricists and vocalists representing a range of musical and linguistic influences. The result is a warm and compelling musical treatise on the diverse cultural history of Brazil, expressed through the Brazilian variant of Portuguese, best described as Brasiliano. Returning to his roots, the opening cut and lead single �A hist�ria de nossa l�ngua� features Gilberto Gil, a national treasure with whom Santtana worked early in his career. As the liner notes explain, Brasiliano , the language, is depicted in the song as a feminine character meeting other people (languages) on her travels, tracing the history of the language as an offshoot of Latin, including �Occitan, Celtic, Galician, Portuguese, Mozarabic, and others. The chorus features Indigenous words that are part of everyday Brazilian culture: Itapu�, Ipanema, Maracan�, Capoeira, etc.� This song acts as a sort of abstract for the dissertation to follow. Santtana and Gil call and respond over what has become the composer�s trademark mixture of detailed, layered, human-played instruments, including on this track violins and violas, piano, guitars, mellotron, and synths. Throughout the record, Santtana creates an inviting effect with a contemporary gloss, combined with the warm resonance of wood, drum skins, wire strings, sticks, bows, and voices. The album features a range of styles, from the lively party track �Ver meu povo se abra�ar� to the convincing reggae of the second single, �Que seja um reggae�. With sophisticated songcraft and inspired arrangements, the songs remain inviting and accessible. Brasiliano by Lucas Santtana Fitting with the theme of the interrelationships among languages, Brasiliano is a celebration of international collaboration. For example, �Independ�ncia� features Karyna Gomes, a singer from Guinea-Bissau; Anglo-French performer Piers Faccini sings �Battre des ailes� accompanied by an appropriately French-sounding accordion; and popular Brazilian singer Flavia Coelho is featured on �Dans le sud feat�. The gentle �Strati di tempo� is the closest to Santtana�s earliest singer/guitarist style, with Italian star Dimartino taking the lead vocals. Brasiliano by Lucas Santtana Language is culture; so too are politics. And with the involvement of Gilberto Gill, who served as Minister of Culture in President Luiz In�cio Lula da Silva�s government and was jailed and exiled for his political affiliations in the 1960s, it is no surprise that this album is overtly political.� For example, on �L�nguas Gerais,� French rapper Oxmo Puccino �speaks about colonization.� Continuing to quote from the liner notes, �Indigenous languages and cultures in South America were buried under European colonization.� Tainara Takua and Oxmo Puccino sing �Cocanha� in Occitan. Their music is part of a movement to prevent this endangered romance language from dying out.� � Like his popular previous recording O Para�so (2023), which was concerned with the environment, Brasiliano is a concept album that explores the role of linguistics in culture. And like on O Para�so , Santtana is never preachy. The high-minded intellectual roots of the project are made palatable by the creative and appealing music assembled to tell the story. It is a message of inclusion, collaboration, and the joy of our shared occupancy in this place and at this time. With many languages, many musical styles, and the artistry of many talented and effective musical partners, Brasiliano is a remarkable achievement in curation and musical skill with a compelling contemporary message. items._cn_summary: Lucas Santtana的《Brasiliano》是一张以巴西语言文化为核心的多语种音乐项目。专辑以葡语、法语、英语、西班牙语、奥克语、佛得角克里奥尔语及巴西原住民图皮-瓜拉尼语演唱，邀请各国音乐人参与合作，Gilberto Gil在开场曲中献声，将巴西葡语描绘为一位女性角色，在旅途中与其他语言相遇，追溯其从拉丁语到当代混合形态的历史。专辑涵盖派对曲风、雷鬼、意大利民谣元素等多种风格，编曲以精细分层的人声演奏为核心，融合小提琴、中提琴、钢琴、吉他、键盘与合成器，木质与鼓皮质感突出。歌曲从热闹的聚会氛围到柔和的歌手吉他质感均有涵盖，政治议题因Gil的参与而显性化，贯穿语言即文化的主线。整体呈现温暖而具邀请感的跨文化音乐论述。

items.body: Photo: Aboubacar Traor� A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking by Neba Solo & Benego Diakit� The newly released album from Malian musicians Neba Solo and Benego Diakit� is the outcome of a project which began in 2013 when Solo and Diakit�, playing balafon and n'goni respectively, were recorded by Bamako producer Ousmane Ha�dara. He played the result to another record producer, Nick Gold, who was completely taken by what he heard and together they decided to work on the recording to produce a finished album, also enlisting English musician Sonny Johns to help with the production. Gold had previously brought together Ali Farka Tour� and Toumani Diabat� to record what was to become the very successful album In the Heart of the Moon and this was a similar story, Solo and Diakit� also being established Malian musicians coming from different musical backgrounds. Indeed, the balafon and n'goni, though both widely associated with Malian music, are seldom played together. A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking , released as a double CD, is very much an album of two halves. The recordings made in 2013 of the two musicians playing together were transformed over time into ensemble arrangements with the addition of other musicians playing strings, mellotron, guitar and percussion, plus overdubbed vocals from Solo and three female singers. These reworked tracks make up the first half of the album. A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking by Neba Solo & Benego Diakit� The opening track, �Djin� Mogo Tiki� begins with a capella backing vocals before Diakit� introduces a repeated riff on the n'goni over which Solo improvises on the balafon while also taking the lead vocal, a pattern which forms the basis of all the tracks, with the augmented instrumentation creating further layers of interest. �Djin� Mogo Tiki� is one of two tracks to have strings added and these sit well, used sparingly to provide short rhythmic motifs, thankfully belying any fears that might be raised by mention of a string arrangement. A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking by Neba Solo & Benego Diakit� The reinvention of these pieces, clearly done with the co-operation of both Solo and Diakit�, may be radical but it has nevertheless been carried out with consideration and musical sensibility. �Yeredon Bali� begins with a few phrases from Solo's balafon, to be joined by Diakit�'s n'goni, some light percussion and hand claps and then more of the female backing vocals, supporting Solo's vocal in the call and response style characteristic of so much Mande music. In this case the vocal content is the only significant addition to the original duo recording, but significant it is because, in the nature of things, once a vocal line is added that becomes the main focus of attention. What makes the format of this album particularly intriguing is that the final six tracks give us the opportunity of hearing the original, unadorned versions of most of the arranged tracks as first recorded by Neba Solo and Benego Diakit�. They are referred to as the �Garden Demos� since they were recorded in a Bamako garden under a mango tree. Without the added vocals the focus shifts to the interplay between the two musicians, and the meaning of the music changes. "Djine Mogo Tiki (Garden Demo excerpt) For example, we are offered two versions of "Djin� Mogo Tiki," first appearing as the album's opening track in its arranged version, then later in the original duo take. Perhaps this has been done to show two sides of the same story, with an awareness too of differences in what audiences are looking for. The arranged tracks, with their instrumental variety and vocal additions, certainly work well and might help give the music wider appeal. But if you are someone who is captivated by listening to fine players engaged in a musical conversation, eavesdropping on the almost telepathic interaction taking place as the two musicians explore the common ground between them, then it's really already there in the earlier Garden Demos, the final six tracks of A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking .

items._cn_summary: 这是一张马里音乐家合作的器乐跨界专辑，以巴拉风琴和恩戈尼为核心乐器，二者虽同为马里传统乐器却鲜少同台。专辑分为两个部分：2013年原始的二重奏录音被重塑，加入弦乐、mellotron、吉他、打击乐以及人声叠加，形成更具层次感的合奏编排。制作人Nick Gold此前曾促成Ali Farka Touré与Toumani Diabaté的合作，此次以类似方式呈现两位背景迥异的成熟音乐家的碰撞。开场曲以无伴奏和声引入，恩戈尼重复音型贯穿，巴拉风琴即兴盘旋其上，弦乐编排克制而恰到好处。多数曲目保留了二重奏的核心结构，仅以人声叠加和打击乐点缀完成扩展。整张专辑虽非激进实验，但在传统马里音乐的框架内展现了器乐对话与编排再构的可能性。

items.excerpt: Tovi by Teija Niku It�s been a lengthy wait for the fourth album from Finnish accordionist Teija Niku, but she�s hardly been idle over the last few years. Between the pandemic, giving birth, and the death of her mother, her time has been filled. But the long pause makes this return all the sweeter, with its joyful exploration of the places where the music of her homeland intersect with her deep love of Balkan music.
items.body: Tovi by Teija Niku It�s been a lengthy wait for the fourth album from Finnish accordionist Teija Niku, but she�s hardly been idle over the last few years. Between the pandemic, giving birth, and the death of her mother, her time has been filled. But the long pause makes this return all the sweeter, with its joyful exploration of the places where the music of her homeland intersect with her deep love of Balkan music. Tovi by Teija Niku That�s amply illustrated on her composition �Finsko Dajchovo,� inspired by the Bulgarian folk dance rhythm, a loving creation that moves sprightly and gracefully, or �Seitsem�n,� taking its cue from Macedonian love songs. The bright, springlike melody, light, full of promise and hope could have been written for eager dancing feet. Everywhere, Niku displays her acute sense of melody. �Elokuu,� a celebration of the late summer lights of August, is a lilting, wistful piece, yet tinged with shades of melancholy for the winter to come, a masterful evocation of shifting moods. Tovi by Teija Niku While the influence of Balkan music hovers over Tovi (the title, according to Niku, translates as �an undefined bit of time, somewhere between a moment and a while�), a Nordic sensibility remains very much at its heart, with a couple of soaring polskas to move things briskly along, in a contrast to the brief, shadowy, brooding opener �Ohto.� Tovi by Teija Niku But the real heart of the disc comes at the very end, with �Poloneesi �idille,� a piece Niku composed for her mother�s 70th birthday, three years before she died. It�s a soft, elegiac work that suddenly becomes transcendent as she begins to sing, You can hear that this performance is completely from the heart, and it is a beautiful way to finish. Now to hope that it�s not such a long gap before she�s back in the studio. Find the artist online. items._cn_summary: 芬兰手风琴演奏家Teija Niku的第四张专辑经历了疫情、生育与丧母等人生变故后姗姗来迟，将北欧民间音乐与巴尔干音乐传统进行深度交融。专辑标题意为'介于瞬间与一段时光之间的未定时间'，体现了她对时间与情感流动的敏锐感知。曲目如'Finsko Dajchevo'取材于保加利亚民间舞蹈节奏，轻快灵动；'Seitsemän'受马其顿情歌启发，旋律明亮如春；'Elokuu'捕捉八月夏末光线中的惆怅与怀旧。整张专辑以北欧气质为底色，穿插几首活泼的波尔卡舞曲，与阴郁短小的开篇形成张力。专辑末尾的'Poloneesi Äidille'是为母亲七十岁生日所作的挽歌，柔美而超脱，人声加入后情感直抵内心，是整张专辑最具分量的时刻。手风琴作为核心乐器贯穿始终，展现出旋律感与叙事性的高度统一。

items.body:
Photo: Claudia de Ventura
Crete�s Stelios Petrakis is at the peak of players of his island�s best-known traditional instrument, the Cretan lyra, a small pear-shaped fiddle held vertically on the knee. Its three bowed strings are stopped by the fingernails of the non-bowing hand rather than being pressed to the fingerboard. Its sound hovers on the enticing edge between fundamental and harmonics.
Petrakis is also a leading luthier, making the lyras and the other instruments he plays, including the traditional metal-strung lute laouto, and in conjunction with Ross Daly he�s developed and plays a range of lyras with ringing sympathetic strings.
True to its title, this an album of his lyra, and laouto, with a panoply of other traditional instruments played by musicians of equal stature to Petrakis, in music of rich lyricism, in melody and texture.
�Astro Sti Gaza� (�Star in Gaza�), a wish for peace written by Petrakis with lyrics by his brother Yannis Petrakis, opens the album. At first a string drone, then Petrakis�s laouto and lyra, Ma�lle Duchemin�s harp, Pavlos Spyropoulos�s double bass, and the percussion of Iranian Bijan Chemirani, who plays frame and flask hand-drums on most tracks. The dark, sinuous instrumental line is tracked by the husky vocal of Giorgis Xylouris, who sings on three tracks, the other six being instrumental. �Nathenas,� a traditional Cretan song in asymmetric rhythms, has a powerful ensemble of lyra, laouto, frame-drum, stick-hit davul, topped out by Breton Sylvain Barou�s reeds and Armenian shvi whistle.
�Anglianico,� a stately melody composed by Petrakis, has the tremolo mandolins of Valencian musician Efr�n L�pez and Michalis Kontaxakis in an elegant almost orchestral sound with lyra, guitars (Antonis Voumvoulakis and Samuel Mele), Spyropoulos�s double bass, and the accordion of Mattia Marco Gregoriadis on whose improvisation the tarantella-like �Pukan� is based.
Chemirani is particularly featured on his composition �Panj Pol,� a short finger-rippling, slapping solo on zarb flask-drum whose rhythm is the foundation for the song that it breaks into, �Agrilos,� by Petrakis with lyrics by brother Yannis celebrating the wine-producing district of Crete where they grew up. It develops into a big sound of massed instruments, with a break on frame-drum and Sakir Oran Uygan�s big double-headed davul drum before a surge of squealing tulum bagpipe and other wind instruments from Barou.
�Evlerin �n� Mersin,� a traditional tune from Asia Minor, has a march-like feel, beginning with keening lyra over a slow, inexorable drum pulse, building to soaring epic as more instruments join, peaking with Barou�s zurnas. �Muixeranga,� again with a steady, imposing pulse, is an anthemic tune played in Valencia during the Muixeranga, the traditional building of excitingly high pyramidal human towers in which the big and strong form the bottom layers and the youngest and lightest clamber up to form the topmost. Petrakis intends the track as a message of support to Valencia following the climate-change-driven floods of 2024.
Preluded and accompanied by ringing 3/4 time arpeggiating plucked strings and percussion, with the melody played on lyra, the source of �Nothing Else Matters,� is unexpected: it�s a beautiful version, evocative of memory and perhaps sadness, of a Metallica number.

items._cn_summary: 克里特音乐家Stelios Petrakis专注于克里特lyra琴与laouto琉特琴的演奏与制作，他与Ross Daly合作开发了带共鸣弦的改良lyra。这张专辑以他的lyra和laouto为核心，汇聚了来自希腊、布列塔尼、亚美尼亚、伊朗、瓦伦西亚、土耳其等地的优秀乐手，跨越地中海与中东文化圈。曲目既有传统克里特民歌与非对称节奏，也有Petrakis本人谱写的庄严旋律与塔兰泰拉式即兴，还包含致敬阿斯图里亚斯人塔传统的进行曲风格作品。乐评细致描述了每首曲目的乐器编制与编曲层次，展现出扎实的传统功底与跨地域协奏的丰富织体，契合世界音乐爱好者的审美。

items.body: The Canterbury event will take place next July JG Thirlwell, AKA Foetus Shadowlands, a new four-day festival at Canterbury's Gulbenkian Arts Centre, has revealed the initial lineup announcement for its inaugural edition in July 2027. The festival will be headed up by JG Thirlwell's Foetus project, performing with a 20-piece chamber orchestra in what will be one of his final live appearances under the moniker. There will also be sets by Lustmord – performing in the UK for the first time in two decades – Test Dept, Regis and Clock DVA. Githead – comprised of Colin Newman of Wire, Malka Spiegel of Minimal Compact, and Robin Rimbaud – are also returning from a 13-year hiatus for the event. The first announcement is rounded out... The post Foetus, Lustmord and More to Play Inaugural Shadowlands Festival in 2027 appeared first on The Quietus.
items._genre: industrial / experimental / dark ambient / post-punk / noise
items._cn_summary: 本文为新音乐节Shadowlands的首届阵容公告，报道了2027年7月于坎特伯雷Gulbenkian艺术中心举行的四天活动。核心亮点为JG Thirlwell的Foetus项目将以二十人室内乐团编制演出，这是该名号下的少数现场亮相之一。Lustmord时隔二十年首次在英国演出，Test Dept、Regis、Clock DVA等工业与电子场景代表人物同台亮相。由Wire主唱Colin Newman等组成的Githead结束十三年休整回归。整体阵容聚焦工业、实验电子、暗潮与后朋克领域的资深音乐人，体现地下场景的传承脉络。本文为纯新闻稿，缺乏音乐评论深度与艺术分析，仅作为演出信息参考。

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以叙事性线索贯穿作品，开篇以男孩与海洋的对话构建出童话般的意境，将听者引入一段关于建造与重建的循环叙事。作曲者似乎借用裁缝与缝制的意象，暗示作品在结构层面的手工感与编织感，每一次聆听都呈现不同的纹理。专辑围绕两位不协调的恋人之间的舞蹈展开，音乐在不同段落之间进行反复重构，营造出剧场化的氛围。整体呈现出当代古典与实验音乐交汇的特点，注重概念表达与声音质地的探索。

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑基于作曲家Liza Lim的《奥瑞斯忒亚》（The Oresteia），将古希腊悲剧题材引入当代古典音乐语境。乐评从1987年欧洲新音乐图景切入，描绘了那个处于六十至七十年代欧洲音乐传统与年轻一代全球化先锋音乐交替之际的创作氛围——欧洲作为文化概念正处于重塑之中，美学观念也在持续更新。Lim以当代作曲手法重构古典神话文本，使古老的叙事框架获得新的音乐表达。文章以历史化的视角将作品置于欧洲先锋音乐版图变迁的脉络中讨论，关注作曲家如何在传统题材与前卫技法之间建立张力。对于关注当代古典音乐谱系演变与实验性歌剧创作的听众而言，这篇乐评提供了有价值的语境信息。

items._cn_summary: ELISION Ensemble 是澳大利亚首屈一指的新音乐乐团，其成员水平可与奥地利的 Klangforum Wien、德国的 MusikFabrik 及法国 Ensemble 等顶级欧洲当代乐团比肩。文中将此次演出描述为超越普通实验范畴的事件，认为简单的报告式记录难以承载其规模与深度。该评论来自专业古典音乐杂志 VAN Magazine，内容关注当代古典音乐领域的前沿实践和现场演出。由于原文内容截断且篇幅过短，无法深入了解具体作品的声音设计、作曲技法或演出细节，因此难以充分评估其创新性和跨领域融合程度。该专辑/演出定位于当代音乐专业领域，与实验音乐和现代作曲密切相关，但评论信息量有限。

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — A Dutch blues-rock jam band who aspired to Kosmische-style jazz-rock music and, in fact, notably were successful at creating their own particular kind of jazz-rock music while coming from Traffic- and The Who-like blues-rock perspectives.1. "Saras Ritt Durch Schwarzwald" (6:23) impressive Who-like Rock approaching Hawkwind-like Prog or Krautrock. I love Johannes Pappert's Arabian/Indian-styled sax play in the fourth and fifth minute's "interlude." The singing (in Dutch) is like a cross between CAN and early Ozzie. (8.75/10)2. "M.C. Escher" (6:14) the organ-base to the first minute of this one makes it feel like URIAH HEEP but then Johannes' sax enters, taking the wind out of the heavy rock vibe. At the end of the second minute the music totally changes (though still using the same instrumental palette): driving rock drums and bass with long-sustained organ chords. A reliance on a set "heavy metal" guitar chord progression is also reminiscent of bands like Heep, Sabbath, Deep Purple, and Nektar. A brief "normal" voiced lyric in the middle is interesting for its educational attempt. (8.6667/10)3. "Kraan Arabia" (9:45) another droning near-"heavy metal" song that is so quintessentially Krautrock is most notable for the way it exploits Johannes' Arabian sounding and melodic sensibilities on his saxophone. There are a couple sound effects switches on the sax and a few windows for Peter Wolbrandt's rhythm guitar and lead guitar to step into the spotlight. And, damn! Hellmut Hattler is a solid and yet fluid bass player. Note the flange effect placed upon the mics recording Jan Fride's cymbals. The laughter and "smoke-break" breakdown in the eighth minute is rather FOCUS- and CAN-like but it also enables Hellmut the chance to solo a bit (not as good of a soloist as rhythmatist) as well as Jan to show off his conga and supplemental percussion instrumental skills while also showcasing more of Peter's guitar skills (also a great rhythmatist). (17.75/20)4. "Head" (18:36) impressive display of rhythmic expression and group unity--especially from Hellmut and Jan. Too bad about the somewhat cheesy riffs borrowed from British rockers like The Who. (35.5/40)5. "Sara auf der Gansewies" (2:01) bluesy cinema music using sax and guitar doubled up to present the plaintive main melody and bass. I like it though it is nothing Earth-shatteringly innovative. (4.375/5)Total Time: 42:59A rock album that draws from a lot of diverse influences including a Krautrock foundation that is heavily steeped in Can-like Kosmische Musik, Steve Winwood organ-based Blues-Rock, The Who's new and more concise Rock 'n' Roll, Chicago Transit Authority jazz-rock, and many of the psychedelic influences that tap into (or arise from) Middle Eastern and Oriental influences. It is also obvious that the band had heard Can, King Crimson, Brainbox/Focus, The Who, and The Mahavishnu Orchestra. Despite their jazzification of a lot of their instrumental performances, the music here feels quite solidly founded in blues-rock structures and motifs--which makes them feel much more akin to bands like The Spencer Davis Group and Traffic. They may have been inspired by The Mahavishnu Orchestra but they sound to me much more like Ash Ra Tempel, Amon D��l II, and/or Can. And, yes: Hellmut Hattler is a GREAT bass player! (How 'bout bringing he and Can's Jaki Liebezeit together with Triumvirat's J�rgen Fritz and Jan Akkerman for a Teutonic super super-group!)B-/3.5 stars; a nice addition to any prog rocker's music collection--especially if s/he is interested in the early foundational music of Krautrock, European Heavy Metal, and/or psychedelic prog.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张1972年荷兰乐队KRAAN的首张专辑，乐评将其定位为一支从布鲁斯摇滚出发、融入宇宙音乐与爵士摇滚元素的乐队作品。专辑中萨克斯风大量采用阿拉伯与印度音阶风格，与键盘、吉他形成跨文化对话，部分曲目引用中东与东方音乐元素。评论特别赞赏贝斯手Hattler兼具稳健与流动性的节奏功底，以及鼓手Fride对镲片话筒加入法兰克效果的处理手法。乐队在编曲中展现出Can式的太空摇滚质感、Focus式的幽默拼贴，以及对The Who与Uriah Heep等英式硬摇滚的致敬。整体制作既有即兴铺陈的器乐段落，也有声效切换与氛围断裂的实验性设计，是欧洲七十年代跨界融合摇滚的典型产物。

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — A second studio album put together in 1971 in London under the supervision of producer Tony Visconti (and also receiving the artistic talents of Roger Dean for the album art).1. "Beautiful Seven" (6:45) some soulful High Life music that has the advantage of Western rock production values to bring about better definition to and performances from each of the individual instruments. (Tony is figuring out how to mic and engineer this band!) The melodies, engineering, and mixes here are so much more superior to anything on the band's previous album (which was released within the same calendar year). The SANTANA-like jam that emerges in the final minute is what I've been looking more for. Still, the overall quality of the sound and performances is so much better than Osibisa. (13.75/15)2. "Y Sharp" (6:21) Memphis Blues-Rock sounding like it's coming straight out of the Stax recording studios--as if Isaac Hayes and David Porter were composing their music! Very enjoyable, nicely-polished mostly-instrumental music of a generic type that the musicians are embellishing with satisfactory spirit and inspiration. (9.125/10) 3. "Spirits Up Above" (7:18) a song that opens up sounding like PROCOL HARUM or THE SPENCER DAVIS GROUP setting up a ballad. But then the unusual tandem of trumpet and flute present the dirge-like melody lines over wah-wah-ed electric guitar and baritone sax. Wow! This is then trumped by the entrance and vocal presence of a church-like "Baptist" choir singing what could be a eulogy for a minute or so. Then the band suddenly kicks into Blues-Rock third gear with a two-chord vamp over which Robert Bailey's electric piano solos over Roy Bedeau and Sol Amarfino's excellent bass and drumming, respectively. Wendel Richardson's guitar solo is next and it's really cool with chord sliding and multi-note picking, all the while the horn section is supporting with its smooth long notes--until the seventh minute when the individual horns start to meander off onto their paths. What an awesome jam! This is by far the best thing I've heard from this band so far! (14.75/15)4. "Survival" (6:19) opening with some in-studio banter before Wendel (at least, I'm assuming it's Wendell) leading the band into a West African drum-and-chant opening (lasting 90 seconds!). I love this! And then at 1:45 the full band joins in, transitioning the music into some Memphis-ized High Life music--one that has some serious funk groovin' coming from Roy and Wendell as well as Robert's full organ chords and the tight horn section's accents and dominating lead melody blasts. In the middle of the fifth minute as Loughty Amao breaks free to solo with his tenor sax the rest of the band breaks into What's Going On-like party mingling noise in the background. Another awesome song! (9.5/10)5. "Move On" (4:34) opening with the "Oh-See-Bee-Sah" chant, the bass and percussion soon jump in with Wendel strumming acoustic guitar in a Django fashion to create a Caribbean-sounding High Life motif over which Wendel sings in a forceful Eric Burdon or Terry Kath-like singing voice and style, which changes the feel of the music into something more akin to War-like Jazz-Rock. Interesting. I like the sound palette, stylistic variety, but overall something's not quite working (besides the slightly murky overall mix). Maybe it's a bit over-filled: too busy; the Rock elements feel a little under-prepared and forced. (8.75/10)6. "Rabiatu" (5:07) a nice African-familiar High Life motif is taken into bluesier territory by all of the electrified instruments: Hammond organ, electric guitar, and watered-down bass line. The percussion line interlude in the third minute is cool--especially with Wendel's percussive rhythm guitar muted strumming and the deep, distant bass lines coming from both Ray's bass and Robert's Hammond. The horn work is very effective--very adeptly arranged. (8.875/10)7. "Woyaya" (4:27) PROCOL HARUM-like Hammond organ chords open this one before Wendel (barely) joins in to start the vocal choir up with his single-voiced recitation of the main lyric and melody, which is thereafter picked up by the whole band as a choir. They sound a bit like they're ending their night in an Irish pub with a drunken sing-a-long of some national (or local) anthem. Once they reach the fourth minute, as the choir join in singing the song title work over and over, things feel quite tight, but then they break into a percussion-only jam to finish it off for the final 45 seconds. Too bad! That "Woyaya" chant could've gone on a bit longer. A cool song--that could very easily be made into a whole-crowd anthem--that feels, to my mind, to be too loosely thrown together and condensed almost unnaturally when it could've been a nice eight or nine minute song. (8.875/10)Total Time: 40:44What a great leap forward for this band! Tony Visconti has figured the band out (proving his genius) and gotten superior sound, spirited performances of inspired compositions from this talented ensemble.A-/five stars; a minor masterpiece of mostly very-well-produced, very well composed African Jazz Rock. Very highly recommended.

items._cn_summary: 这张1971年的专辑由伦敦制作的加纳乐队Osibisa录制，融合了西非Highlife、灵魂乐、孟菲斯蓝调摇滚和爵士元素。制作人Tony Visconti提升了录音品质，Roger Dean负责封面艺术。乐曲在高life律动与西方摇滚制作之间取得平衡，铜管组与电吉他、键盘形成层次丰富的对话。《Spirits Up Above》以类似教堂唱诗班的伴唱开场，随后转入蓝调摇滚即兴，融合了Procol Harum式的庄严与Santana式的放克段落。《Survival》展现西非鼓乐与孟菲斯风格放克的交织。《Y Sharp》则带有Stax录音室式的灵魂乐质感。整体上，专辑将非洲传统节奏与摇滚乐队的编制巧妙结合，是世界音乐与摇滚融合领域的一次成功尝试。

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — A newly-formed band of West African-born musicians get together in a London studio to try to create music for a studio album. The sessions had the support of up-and-coming producer Tony Visconti (The Move, Procol Harum, T. Rex, David Bowie, Magna Carta, Gentle Giant, Strawbs) and the album cover the art work of the one and only Roger Dean! Osibisa was released by MCA Records in June of 1971.1. "Dawn" (7:03) built over a two-chord bass and guitar vamp, the horns and percussion section start out rather tamely while Teddy Osei vocalizes in West African fashion beneath the soloing instruments (Hammond organ, electric guitar, flute, ). Of all the soloists only the first, Robert Bailey's Hammond organ, feels truly inspired, the rest feel as if they're just going through the motions of a song they've played a million times and feel bored performing in the relatively-unresponsive confines of a studio. (I'm suggesting that this song probably goes over bigger in a live concert setting.) (13/15)2. "Music for Gong Gong" (5:29) presenting a sound that feels more Caribbean-familiar, the horns feel quite engaged as does Robert Bailey's organ (once again). The rest of the band feels as if they're moving through rudiments, coming off a previous night's bender with some sluggishness and, perhaps, a slight hangover. The two two-chord vamp progressions lack the inspired embellishments that, say, a Santana or Mandrill might add. The highly-touted percussionists finally start to show some life (and spirit) in the second half of the fourth minute (when the rest of the instruments back out). (8.75/10)3. "Ayiko Bia" (7:53) from the very opening call-and-response chants this one feels fully-engaged, fully-representative of African High Life music. The rhythm section is next to expose their shtick before the horns add a kind of Memphis Horns layer. Then the organ-based music breaks open a different, softer approach to the opening's call-and-response, making this the main motif for the song to build itself around. At 2:40 the organ swirls and the horns activate as we enter an instrumental section for some guitar soloing from Wendel Richardson. So far, Robert Bailey is really the only instrumentalist in the band that really impresses me: the dude is so engaged and so creative. Mac Tontoh gets the next solo with his trumpet as the response choir activates as if the trumpet is now their call master. Then, around 5:30 we get another break from textural instruments so that the percussionists can have a party. I like these sections (but then I'm a sucker for all percussion polyrhythmic weaves). (13.375/15)4. "Akwaaba" (4:20) borrowing from American New Orleans blues-jazz the band establishes a weave that feels similar to the previous song in terms of the instrumentation populating it but the mood and vibe feels quite different: much more Americanized. Even the melody lines used by the horns, organ, and lead guitar are far more similar to the fare coming out of Western/American blues artists. A little too bland and studio suppressed to excite me. At the end of the song the four chord progression is repeated over and over with the vocal choir shouting out the letter-by-letter spelling of the band's name before the horn sections group blasts finish things off. (8.75/10)5. "Oranges" (4:40) another song that feels quite founded in American blues music (like Wilson Pickett)--until 1:15 when trumpeter Mac Tontoh is set up for a solo (over some more-circumscribed Wilson Pickett-like drum-and-bass music). The choir joins in, sometimes working in two groups (or two tracks) repeating the song name over and over before a brief sax bridge unveils a thinned out passage over which Wendell lays down a solid Southern Blues-Rock guitar solo. Robert's electric piano work in the mid-range is quite interesting. (8.75/10)6. "Phallus C" (7:14) "fallacy" is really what they're saying as they put together a fairly simple High Life blues root over which the vocalists call-and-response approach tells the story of being misjudged according to stereotypes. The work of the horn players, especially Loughty Amao's baritone sax, as well as Robert's under-volumed Hammond and Wendell's aggressive Rock electric guitar, are all notable and respectable. I only wish the overall result were a little better. (13.375/15)7. "Think About the People" (4:21) starting out quite quietly as bass, percussionists, organ, and guitar all seem to be finishing their tuning and warm ups. Nearly a minute into the recording does anything congeal into forward motion. What results is a CURTIS MAYFIELD-like High Life tune with more social-consciousness lyrics about the need for revolution. At 2:25 the music segues into a brief kind of crescendo-acting motif (which may or may not be meant as a chorus) before the band returns to a pepped up version of the Curtis motif before disintegrating into . . . lights out. Time to go! (8.75/10)Total Time: 41:36Overall I have to say that this well-regarded band's debut studio album is highly underwhelming. I perceive that these songs may receive quite an injection of adrenaline (and enthusiasm) when performed in front of a live audience but they need to do something to get that actively-engaged spirit to come through in these studio recordings! (Is producer Tony Visconti to blame? Was the band's unusual instrumental palette too new for him?)C-/2.5 stars; a collection of sadly disappointing music that seems to lack inspiration and/or full engagement. For collectors only.

items._cn_summary: 这张1971年的专辑由西非裔音乐人在伦敦录制，是非洲节奏与爵士摇滚融合的早期典范。评论详细追踪了每首曲目的乐器编排与情绪走向，特别注意到哈蒙德风琴手Robert Bailey的演奏在全片中最为投入且富有创意，而部分段落中其他乐手的表现则显得敷衍。打击乐段落被认为是专辑最出彩的部分，多节奏编织充满活力。专辑邀请了Roger Dean设计封面，Tony Visconti担任制作，在制作资源上颇具规格。整体音乐融合了西非Highlife、加勒比律动与新奥尔良爵士蓝调元素，但评论者认为乐队在录音室环境中的表现不如现场，且部分段落缺乏Santana或Mandrill那样的即兴灵气。文字末尾被截断，评论未能完整呈现。

items.excerpt: Review by Fercandio46 — Miaou's second album is titled Make These Things Alright; for it, they doubled down on their fusion of sequenced tracks and live instrumentation, mixing the two in the studio in the style of Saint Etienne, who were also a trio.On "Future Pavilion," Tatsuki Hamasaki's guitar enters the mix; combined with Hiromi Hasegawa's drum groove, playing over Mayumi Hasegawa's cloud of synthesizers feels like performing somewhere it never rains, close to the sun.In *A Bird In Th
items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — Miaou's second album is titled Make These Things Alright; for it, they doubled down on their fusion of sequenced tracks and live instrumentation, mixing the two in the studio in the style of Saint Etienne, who were also a trio.On "Future Pavilion," Tatsuki Hamasaki's guitar enters the mix; combined with Hiromi Hasegawa's drum groove, playing over Mayumi Hasegawa's cloud of synthesizers feels like performing somewhere it never rains, close to the sun.In *A Bird In The Hand*, they opt for a pattern of repetition and counterpoint; however, while their starting point is reminiscent of Stereolab, the extended melodic development, which always sounds alternative and modern, subsequently leads them toward the East. It is esoteric and provocative, even in its calmness."Silent Picture" unfolds in a near-psychedelic manner, reminiscent of Air, whereas "Tiger Note" is more energetic, shifting into a sound akin to The Breeders, complete with distortion."On A Sunday," by contrast, achieves an almost dreamlike, progressive atmosphere, evoking the ballads King Crimson crafted in the early 90s. The guitarist conjures a special aura with his notes, elevating the entirety of "Make These Things Alright" and bathing it in a radiant, rainbow-like glow. The premise of blending technology with indie rock had previously leaned too heavily toward Sonic Youth, but with "When Will You Come Home?", that fusion returned in all its glory, suspending time... and stopping the clocks in its wake.LASA reminded me of the Smashing Pumpkins, despite being instrumental, because that specific type of distortion, layered with something else underneath, is present in Miaou's sound; it acts as a bridge connecting the 90s to the early 2000s, eras that share so much in common, much like the tonal nuances offered by the trio.
items._genre: post-rock / math rock / electronic fusion / indie
items._cn_summary: MIAOU的第二张专辑《Make These Things Alright》以三人组合的形式展开，将序列化的电子音轨与现场乐器演奏在录音室中实时混合，延续了Saint Etienne式的制作思路。滨崎达行的吉他与长谷川广美的鼓组在长谷川真由美的合成器云层之上展开对话，使整体听感介于Stereolab式的重复与对位与东方旋律延展之间，在平静中带有神秘色彩。部分曲目接近迷幻氛围，吉他音色营造出彩虹般的光泽；另一些段落则加入了失真处理，向九十年代独立摇滚倾斜。整张专辑试图在技术与摇滚之间找到平衡点，将九十年代另类吉他音乐与千禧年初的电子元素进行桥接，呈现出一种跨越时代质感的器乐表达。

items.body: Swans, the New York post-industrial and experimental rock group led by Michael Gira, will release “Newly Sentient Being” on 2 October 2026 through Mute / Young God Records (North America). The record documents Swans’ final “Big Sound” performance, played in Berlin on 28 November 2025, and comes as a 4-vinyl + DVD set with poster, a double CD + DVD with fold-out booklet, and digitally. “Newly Sentient Being” documents the closing concert of the lineup that toured as Swans from 2010 to 2025: Michael Gira, Kristof Hahn, Dana Schechter, Larry Mullins, Phil Puleo, Christopher Pravdica and Norman Westberg. The Berlin show ran over two and a half hours across just five songs, and the recordings include material never previously released. A DVD of the full performance, directed by Marco Porsia and Peter Harton, is included with the vinyl and CD editions. The tracklist for “Newly Sentient Being” runs “The End of Forgetting,” “The Merge,” “Paradise Is Mine,” “Newly Sentient Being” and “The End of Regretting.” Beats Per Minute reviewed the Berlin concert, writing: “What followed were over two and a half hours of music, in total just five songs with an intensity and euphoric density that eclipsed that of the previous Gira-led shows I witnessed. In emotional intensity, the concert was often closer to a tribal ritual than musical expression usually allows.” Gira described the decision to close this era of the band in a statement: “In 2010 I made the decision to reconvene my band, Swans, which I had, years earlier, killed out of frustration, disappointment and exhaustion. Now, I saw a light, a way forward for the music, and I decided to pursue it. […] I believe we reached some pretty tremendous highs along the way, where the music became a raging, sentient autonomous beast that played us (and the audience/listener), rather than the reverse. That was the goal all along, to lose ourselves in the swirl. […] Now this phase is finished. There’s nowhere else to take it, but we seem to have ended on a particularly high note with our final tour of this (now passing) Swans era, and I believe these current recordings convey the sensations and experience of the unique world we forged. For the next phase, I’m moving Swans into something with a decidedly more humble, and intimate musical palette, but here now I offer my praise to the righteous group of humans, the musicians that made our final foray into the sonic ether a reality: Norman Westberg, Dana Schechter, Phil Puleo, Larry Mullins, Kristof Hahn, Christopher Pravdica, and I was in there flailing somewhere too.” Watch an excerpt from the performance below. Swans close the 2010-2025 era with ‘Newly Sentient Being’ “Newly Sentient Being” follows Swans’ seventeenth studio album, “Birthing”, released in May 2025, and the European and UK tour the band launched that October to support it, covered by Side-Line in “Swans launch European tour”. The Berlin performance captured on “Newly Sentient Being” marked the end of that touring cycle and of the lineup formed when Gira reconvened Swans in 2010. About Swans Michael Gira founded Swans in New York City in 1982. The early band built a reputation for relentless, high-volume performances, abject imagery in Gira’s lyrics, and thundering vocals, documented on the albums “Filth” and “Cop.” Swans then moved into the harsh, mechanical proto-industrial rock of its Greed period, before combining haunted atmospheres and martial rhythms on the 1987 double album “Children of God.” “The Burning World,” released in 1989, brought gentler, acoustic-based material. After relocating to Atlanta, the band built dense, melody-driven sonic works on “White Light from the Mouth of Infinity” (1991) and “Love of Life” (1993), turning more dissonant and sharp-edged on “The Great Annihilator” (1994). “Soundtracks for the Blind” (1996) drew together all of these strands across more than two hours of music, closing that chapter of the band; Gira disbanded Swans after 15 years of continuous recording and touring. For the following 13 years, Gira recorded under his own name and as Angels of Light. He reconvened Swans in 2010, beginning a second era that ran through 2025 and produced further studio albums, including “The Beggar” (2023) and “Birthing” (2025), along with international touring documented in the 2023 biopic “Where Does a Body End?”. “Newly Sentient Being” documents the final performance of that lineup and marks the end of the 2010-2025 era of the band.
items._cn_summary: 本文为Swans乐队宣布发行现场专辑兼终章之作"Newly Sentient Being"的新闻稿。专辑记录了2025年11月28日在柏林举行的"Big Sound"系列最终演出，五首曲目总时长超过两个半小时，呈现出仪式感与密集声响交织的听觉体验。这场演出标志着2010至2025年间该阵容的终结，成员包括Michael Gira、Norman Westberg、Dana Schechter等七位乐手。录音包含此前未发行的素材，并附有完整演出的DVD。Gira在声明中回顾了重组乐队的心路历程，强调音乐曾如"自主的有机体"般操控演奏者与听众。文章引用了Beats Per Minute的评论，将这场演出比作"部落仪式"。（注：原文为新闻发布性质的资讯，缺少深度乐评分析。）

items.body:
2023 Reissue of the very first Buddha Machine, newly upgraded with better sound quality and user experience including a louder speaker and 2 new individual side buttons to make the device control more direct and intuitive. Available in 5 colours.

You either know what these are and have already hit the buy button, or you’re too young to remember the Brian Eno-fuelled craze for these ambient boxes and are about to enter a portal to a different time. We must have sold several - many - thousands of these in their various iterations, including editions made in collab with Philip Glass and Throbbing Gristle, and after about a decade in the wilderness, they’re now back, in a new replica version of the very first edition from 2005 - that’s before the Iphone era - with improved controls and sound quality. oh, and that all important line out, for your buddha boxing!

In 2005 the Beijing-based duo of Christiaan Virant and Zhang Jian released their first, soon to be iconic  “Buddha Machine” loop box, a quirky pocket soundsystem that propelled sound art into the consumer mainstream. It spawned a whole cultural movement, fuelled by Brian Eno professing his love for them, and an era of live show "Buddha Boxing" improvisations.

The original version has been long sold-out and fetches crazy prices second hand, followed by various further iterations made in collaboration with Philip Glass and Throbbing Gristle. This new edition is a replica of the very fiest version, featuring the original loops in all their 8-bit Lo-Fi glory and available in 5 different colours.

"The classic loops of the original FM3 Buddha Machine evoke instant nostalgia for a slower, more simple world. Born before the iPhone era, this iconic device has weathered two decades of pop culture and fashion trends, yet remains defiantly, heroically unique. Its enduring simplicity cloaks an extraordinary power: the ability to transcend time. It is both a sonic portal to a hands-on analogue past and a bridge to a digital ever-present. This is not just a re-issue; it is a revival and refinement of a sonic manifesto that unfolds softly, gently and organically, resonating with the subtle rhythms of life. The Buddha 1 2023 edition from FM3. Available in 5 colours: Red, Orange, Green, Blue and limited-edition Pink. Features upgraded sound quality and user experience. Louder speaker and 2 new individual side buttons make device control more direct and intuitive."

The Buddha Machine is a truly unique musical device that prefers to sit in the background, quietly and gently working its sonic magic.

*Batteries not included!!!*

items._cn_summary: 本文是对FM3 2005年经典循环播放器Buddha Machine 2023复刻版的介绍。文章回顾了这款由北京艺术家Christiaan Virant与张荐创作的便携式环境音乐设备的文化影响，指出Brian Eno的推崇使其从声音艺术圈走入大众视野，并催生了现场即兴表演形式。该复刻版忠实还原了原始8位低保真循环音色，改进了扬声器音量与侧边按键操作，并新增了线路输出功能。文章整体偏向产品描述与历史回顾，缺乏深入的声音设计分析或音乐评论。作为融合了环境音乐、极简主义循环与低保真音色的硬件装置，Buddha Machine在实验电子音乐史上具有标志性地位，但其复刻性质决定了它在创新维度上的局限性。

items.body:
A perennial reminder to the raw-ass bluesy soul house stomp and wiggle of the GOATy two-part debut album by Detroit/Chicago legend Theo Parrish.

Now of a 28 year vintage, the ultimate collection of woodcut drums, burnished keys and soul-fired vibes in ‘First Floor’ (1998) have aged like a cask oak-steeped single malt whiskey. It’s now a contemporary classic touchstone for deep house at its earthiest and most spirited, depicting Theo locked into signature offbeat grooves that have buried themselves deep under the skin and soundtracked countless late night soirées.

Future-proofed by its uniquely loose but taut knit of minimalist elements worked to jazzwise, hypnotic effect, you can practically taste the sweet smoke and tang in the air of each cut, spanning the lip-bitingly strong, heads-down hustle of ‘First Floor Metaphor’ at the front, thru the timeless deep house immanence of ’Sky Walking’ at the back. In between, ‘Sweet Sticky’ works nagging organ vamps and nattiest drums into a proper stank-face trample, next to the honeyed chords of ‘Paradise Architects’, classic sampler magick in ‘Love Is war For Miles’, a ‘JB’s Edit’ for the wall-bangers, and 10 mins of limb-unravelling tekkerz on ‘Dark Patterns’. Plus, obviously ‘Heal Yourself & Move’ the deepest alltimer, a track that feels almost like a second skin at this point.

It’s one of those albums that’s truly transcends generic borders to influence heads of all stripes with its unmistakeable, soul-nuzzling texture and groove. One for the ages, we tell thee.
items._genre: deep house / soul house / jazz-influenced electronic
items._cn_summary: 这张1998年发行的双部分专辑首部，记录了底特律/芝加哥传奇人物Theo Parrish在deep house领域的标志性创作。乐评强调其木质感鼓机、打磨过的键盘音色与灵魂乐氛围的融合，整体结构松散却紧密，以极简元素编织出爵士式的催眠效果。曲目横跨强劲律动、深沉教堂感、粘腻的管风琴即兴段落与采样拼贴技艺，时长十分钟的techno向作品'暗纹'展现肢体解构式律动。这张专辑被描述为超越流派边界、以独特灵魂质感影响各类听众的时代之作，被视为deep house领域当代经典基准之一。

items.body:
First re-pressing in years of Mark Ernestus & Moritz Von Oswald’s divine, final Rhythm & Sound release, heeling to tradition with a one-riddim album focussed on its carousel of roots reggae legends; Sugar Minott, Paul St. Hilaire, Willi Williams, Jah Cotton, Bobbo Shanti, and more

In 2005 Rhythm & Sound capped their holy mountain catalogue with ‘See Mi Yah’, a 7 x 7” set and LP which completed a 10 year run of inspired dub productions with their purest offering to the form. At the time, younger ears to their music would be left perplexed by the lack of instrumental variation - but any others with a little knowledge of one-riddim set traditions knew it was their ultimate ode to roots reggae fundamentals, after respectfully messing with the style & pattern across the Burial Mix 10”s (as collected in ‘w/ The Artists’), and the more radical 12” mutations of the Rhythm & Sound series, proper, since 1996 (not to mention birthing dub house-techno before that).     

Seeing off the project in fine style, Ernestus & Von Oswald gave studio time to their favourite vocalists, generating a slew of original performances displaying the range and depth of roots reggae’s elders and contemporary torch carriers on their signature backdrop of air-trodding bass and powdered dub chords. We were blessed to distribute it in the UK at the time, so many of these cuts are hard etched to the memory, from the ghostly croon of Willi Williams’ title piece thru the gruff gravitas of Bobbo Shanti, the duet between Ras Donovan & Ras Perez, and of course Sugar Minott’s mellifluous reggae soul.

In the year following ‘See Mi Yah’, Rhythm & Sound were naturally elected to edit and master a re-up of The Congos & Friends’ one-riddim album ’Fisherman Style’ for our then warehouse neighbours Blood & Fire Records, sealing their era of roots reflection by appropriately saluting the originators, in parallel to their Wackies reissue scheme, and before Ernestus (and Mark Ainley) would go on to found the more digi-devoted reissue label, Dug Out. Some 20 years of satisfaction later, time has proven this album holds its meditative weight.
items._cn_summary: 这是Rhythm & Sound组合的收官之作，以一套七首7寸单曲加LP的形式集中呈现roots reggae根基。整张专辑只使用一个riddim节奏，由Sugar Minott、Paul St. Hilaire、Willi Williams等六位牙买加歌手轮流演唱，延续了他们自1996年以来将dub与电子、house、techno相融合的脉络，最终回归最纯粹的dub制作形式。制作人Mark Ernestus与Moritz Von Oswald延续了低音厚实、混响绵密、空间感强烈的dub美学，舍弃编曲变化，以单一节奏承载不同声音的演绎。专辑发行二十年后仍被视为他们对根源雷鬼传统的致敬之作，也标志着一段dub再诠释时代的终结。

items.body:
Formally known as Rabbitfoot, 1000 Rabbits survey their first months and years of activity on this brittle six-track EP.

Since they first assembled in Aldeburgh two years back, 1000 Rabbits have tracked from living room to rehearsal space to stage, working through ideas and concepts to come up with a tight selection of experimentally-minded art pop that should appeal to fans of Wet Leg and Black Country New Road. If you've come across the band before, you've probably run into 'Virgin Soil' a featherlight fusion of staccato string plucks, time signature switches and orchestral swells that sits at odds with vocalist River's nonchalant recollections. 'Rubiks Cube' expands the concept a little more, adding a proggy synth low-end and more elaborate drumming, but it's the non singles that convince us that 1000 Rabbits are more than a novelty name. Peep the gossamer 'Bear Hunt', that sounds as if it coulda come from Clarissa Connelly's 'World of Work', or the lengthy, folk-flecked finale 'Spring Cleaning'.
items._genre: experimental art pop / chamber pop / progressive folk
items._cn_summary: 1000 Rabbits（原名 Rabbitfoot）以这首六曲 EP 回溯成团初期的探索轨迹。乐队从奥尔德堡的客厅起步，逐步进入排练空间与舞台，作品将断弦弹拨、变换拍号与管弦乐起伏编织成实验性艺术流行。点睛之作并非已发行的单曲，而是轻盈如纱的《Bear Hunt》，其质地令人联想到 Clarissa Connelly 的《World of Work》；终曲《Spring Cleaning》则拉长篇幅，融入民谣色调。整体呈现学院派出身对结构与配器的把控，弦乐与合成器低频并置，鼓组推进繁复但克制，展现出超越猎奇标签的创作潜力。

items.body:
Low End Activist proves his ductile production mettle on a rugged dancehall bullet backed with fierce Low Jack & Loraine James remixes for his personal folio.

On the sibling imprint to Low End Activist’s Sneaker Social Club, ‘Invite Chaos (Kill Dem) squares up Vybz Kartel affiliate, Sikka Rymes, on a type of militant dancehall located shades away from The Bug or shots fired on Duppy Gun Productions. items.body:
Another transmission from Naarm's fertile underground, 'The Key to the World' is the third offering (and first outside of Australia) from wyrd pop eccentric Sam Perry and features a cover of Lana Del Rey's 'Mariner's Apartment Complex'.

There's a DIY character to this one that feels totally intentional. The album was recorded in home studios peppered across the world: one in Belgrade, one in Christchurch and one at home in Melbourne. And it's ramshackle without being too disjointed, rolling from short, baroque interludes to bona-fide electro pop bangers at the drop of the hat. Even in a single track, Perry's able to burn down the borders between his influences, casting a glance to Prefab Sprout and Syd Barrett on the ace 'Life's A Party' before it dissolves into a chaos of tape-fluxed euphoria. 'Lake of Ice' comes off like a lost cue from one of Werner Herzog's '80s features and then there's that Lana Del Rey cover, of course.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由澳大利亚Naaram地下场景的Sam Perry发行，录音分散于贝尔格莱德、基督城和墨尔本的家庭工作室，带有刻意为之的DIY粗糙感。音乐在短促巴洛克间奏与电子流行之间跳跃，单首曲目内能跨越Prefab Sprout、Syd Barrett等影响，融合磁带故障美学与崩解式狂喜。曲目'Lake of Ice'令人联想到赫尔佐格八十年代电影配乐，另附Lana Del Rey翻唱。整体呈现一种离经叛道的原创声音，以低保真与跨国远程协作为特色，介于实验流行与地下独立之间。

items.body:
Good Morning Tapes back with a new album of lushest New Age sound-bathing x emotionally gooey trip hop from Andro Gogibedashvili aka Saphileaum, delivered in a mode that’s highly tipped for anyone on the line from Enigma to All Saints, from a.s.o to Boards of Canada.

Saphileaum has spent the past decade in passage between notable houses of atmospheric sorcery - Mule Musiq, Not Not Fun, Slow Life, Constellation Tatsu - and of course Good Morning Tapes, who now host their 3rd meeting, ‘Heavenly Hills’. A definitive chapter in his ten year saga, it is flush with symphonic strings and sky born keys, breezily urged by percussion that straddles chill out and folk zones. That said there’s also a Balearic - or should that be Black Sea? - appeal to its title tune, that lingers in the glistening wake of ‘Your Grace’, to the shimmering breaks of a parting piece ‘Alarko (Cosmic Eagle)’, falling into the space between Boards of Canada's cult-inspired hauntological nostalgia and Shackleton's hallowed ethno-dub.

“The tracks in the album were written with the inspiration of the kingdom of Shambhala in the Himalayas. I'm deeply fascinated and touched by it. Even the album title, holds the idea of its Heavenly nature and the tracks are like individual, elemental parts of it. The album is not a journey into Shambhala, but rather a play and a dance with its energy, image and presence in my world. Alarko (Cosmic Eagle) is dedicated to my grandfather, Temur Tsiklauri, and I dedicate the whole album to my country Georgia, which I deeply love.”
items._genre: new age / ambient / trip hop / electronic
items._cn_summary: Saphileaum 的《Heavenly Hills》是一张融合新纪冥想氛围与trip hop律动的电子专辑，交由小厂牌 Good Morning Tapes 发行。作曲家以喜马拉雅香巴拉王国为创作灵感，试图在音乐中描绘那片理想境域的灵性能量与图景。制作上运用了管弦弦乐与天穹般的键盘音色，鼓点行走在冥想放克与民谣律动之间，标题曲带有地中海巴利阿里式的日光质感，而终曲则引入碎拍结构，浮游于Boards of Canada式的怀旧与Shackleton的民族学dub之间。专辑是作曲家十年来在 Mule Musiq、Not Not Fun、Slow Life 等独立厂牌间辗转创作的阶段性总结，终曲献给他的祖父，整张专辑献给故乡格鲁吉亚，蕴含着个人化的文化情感投射。整体而言，作品呈现的是一种柔软、感性的氛围拼贴，适合午后聆听而非深度的声音实验探索。

items.body:
Steve Gurley and co.’s deeply inspirational run of ’92-’93 hardcore jungle 12”s as Foul Play, compiled on a deadly doublepack via Bristol-via-Berlin torch carriers, Sneaker Social Club.

‘Origins’ contains some of the greatest music of the early ‘90s, particularly spotlighting the transition from rave’s rugged building blocks into artfully hi-tech dance music during that pivotal period. Sifting gems from both volumes of Foul Play’s early EPs on Oblivion Records - including the all-timers ‘Dubbing You’ and ‘Ricochet’ - plus an early 12” for Moving Shadow, the set documents breakbeat hardcore hitting a creative zenith of hyper-chopped soul, dub and pop samples arranged with staccato stabs, cut-up, shuffling breaks and drum machines, right in the pocket before it was codified as jungle. 

Thanks to the studio ingenuity of Steve Gurley, who cut his teeth on these recordings, the set can also be heard to characterise the development of what is known as the hardcore continuum, as defined in Gurley’s subsequent shift into jungle, proper, and then UKG - the ultimate refinement of hardcore’s 2-step shuffles and sexy swerve. The seeds of enduring styles & patterns to come are sown here, from the fractious rush of ‘Finest Illusion’ through the haunting zinger ‘Dubbing You’, to the needlepoint discipline of ‘Ricochet’ and effortless, toes-off-the-floor skip and parry of ‘Screwface’, to the jump-up jungle blueprint ‘Ragatere’.

Alltimers, the lot of them.
items._genre: hardcore jungle / breakbeat hardcore / oldschool rave
items._cn_summary: 这张双碟合辑收录了Foul Play在1992至1993年间于Oblivion Records及Moving Shadow发行的早期单曲，聚焦于硬核丛林诞生的关键转折期。Steve Gurley的录音室手法将碎拍硬核推向了创作巅峰——高度切碎的灵魂、dub与流行样本，配合断奏式的刺音、剪切处理、shuffling碎拍与鼓机节奏，在尚未被正式归类为丛林之前，已展现出精密的拼贴美学。曲目如'Dubbing You'与'Ricochet'以精准的音色控制著称，'Finest Illusion'呈现焦躁的紧迫感，'Ragatere'则预示了jump-up丛林的雏形。这套作品被视为硬核连续体发展史中的重要节点，记载了rave粗糙根基向高技术舞曲转变的过程。Bristol与柏林交汇的Sneaker Social Club厂牌以独立姿态呈现了这批地下经典。

items.body:
'Dragging A Dead Deer Up A Hill’, originally issued by Type in 2008, saw Liz Harris’ now much-loved project take a leap from the filtered, tape-fuelled obfuscation of her earlier releases into the sort of smudged dream-pop soundworld she's now best known for. Trust when we tell you that before this record came out we struggled to sell Grouper albums no matter how much we loved them. This album changed everything.

'Dragging A Dead Deer...' is far more resonant and upfront about its songs than any Grouper material that preceded it. Opening track 'Disengaged' offers a segue of cloudy, amorphous output into a mass of mesmerising magnetic hiss and soft noise, before Harris' guitar and voice finally emerge, reverberant and phantom-like, and yet - finally - comprehensible. 

If you've previously struggled to make out Grouper lyrics, 'Heavy Water/I'd Rather Be Sleeping' offers a way in. Those dense recording techniques had become a unique production signature to the extent that it was virtually impossible to separate Harris' creative identity from that uniquely ghostly sound of hers. But on 'Dragging A Dead Deer...’ it felt like a conduit to her songs, rather than a barrier.

There are echoes of her earlier work too, on the wordless atmospherics of 'Wind & Snow', but the overall impression is one of inspired creative renewal, and the unveiling of a songwriting talent that was previously content to dwell in the shadows, deflecting attention with smoke and mirrors.
items._cn_summary: Grouper的《Dragging a Dead Deer Up a Hill》标志着Liz Harris从早期磁带失真和滤波模糊的创作手法向更清晰的梦幻流行转变。专辑保留了磁带嘶声、柔软噪声和无歌词氛围音景等实验元素，如《Wind & Snow》中纯氛围的段落，但整体呈现出更直白的歌曲结构与人声，吉他和嗓音以幽灵般的混响形态浮现。Harris的演唱终于变得可辨识，让原本被密集录音技术遮蔽的旋律与歌词得以传达。整体听感介于氛围音乐与梦幻流行之间，融合了磁带实验的颗粒质感与独立民谣的简朴旋律，作为她创作生涯的关键转折点，揭示了一位此前倾向于隐藏在烟雾般的声响屏障之后、最终走向光亮的词曲创作者。

items.body: I wasn’t really looking for death I was just looking for myself Six months after the release of Christine Plays Viola’s 2026 album F.I.V.E. (Fear Increases Violent Emotions), the Italian darkwave and post-punk band returns to complete its story. Their latest single “At Last, I Found You” was recorded during the album sessions but deliberately held back, allowing the record’s emotional course to reach listeners before its final companion piece appeared. “At Last, I Found You” begins with synthesizers sighing like brakes slowing a car on a wet road. A low drone hangs behind them until the bass establishes forward momentum, the drums lock into place, and an insistent guitar hook cuts through the gathering pressure. The song soon settles into the kind of danceable gothic rock Christine Plays Viola handle so well: immediate enough for the club, yet weighted with genuine psychic anguish. During the verses, the instruments pull back around the dark, smoldering vocal while bass and drums continue to propel the song beneath faint synthesizers. When the refrain of “break me up, break me up” takes hold, the arrangement surges upward. The guitars broaden, the rhythm bears down, and the vocal rises from exhausted confession into a passionate cry. Direct, memorable, and emotionally severe, it stands among the band’s finest songs to date. The song describes the urge to drive away as an act of self-erasure. After burying the keys to a box containing his dreams, vocalist Massimo Ciampani sings of driving into the night, although he is already convinced that some part of him has died. Cigarette ash, blood, chains, a ditch, and the void surround a man who can no longer recognize himself. Yet the apparent second person referred to in the title gradually assumes another identity. The “you” he has been seeking is his childhood self: the innocence and possibility he abandoned somewhere along the way. The final admission—“I wasn’t really looking for death, I was just looking for myself”—recasts the song’s death drive as a desperate attempt at psychological recovery. By restoring the album’s full title in parentheses, “At Last, I Found You” brings the F.I.V.E. cycle back to its central concern: the point at which fear turns inward, distorts emotion, and threatens to destroy the person carrying it. Guitarist and bandleader Fabrizio Giampietro explains: “At Last, I Found You was always the most immediate and instinctive song we wrote during the F.I.V.E. sessions. We deliberately left it off the album because we wanted listeners to experience that record’s emotional arc without this song becoming its centre of gravity. Six months later, it felt like the right moment to finally share it.” The accompanying video transfers that crisis to a rain-swept nocturnal drive. A leather-jacketed man grips the steering wheel as vacant commercial streets pass beneath violet, red, and electric-blue light. Rain crowds the windows, cigarette smoke fills the cabin, and the camera repeatedly glances toward the empty back seat, leaving a conspicuous space for the person invoked by the song’s title. As the drive continues, the city begins losing its physical certainty. Light bends across the windshield, the road appears to warp, and black mist gathers around the car as the driver’s composure gives way to panic. His gestures become increasingly frantic while flashes of red and blue appear through the rain, suggesting either an approaching police confrontation or another fragment of his unraveling mind. After stopping the car, he steps into the downpour and finds a boy in a blue raincoat waiting across the road. The child stands motionless, staring back at him with an expression that offers neither recognition nor judgment. It is the video’s clearest answer to the lyrics, yet the encounter never establishes whether the boy is a memory, a hallucination, a chance at salvation, or an image seen at the instant of death. The street empties once again, and an overhead view shows the black mist closing around the abandoned car. The video then returns to the back seat, where a small toy car rests beneath the closing credits—the only physical trace of the childhood the driver has spent the night pursuing. He may have found the boy, but finding him and saving him remain two different acts. Watch the video for “At Last, I Found You” below: “At Last, I Found You (Fear Increases Violent Emotions)” is out now through Bandcamp, Spotify, and all major digital platforms. Christine Plays Viola will continue supporting F.I.V.E. with European appearances running from August through October, including dates in Poland, Spain, England, and Germany. Further performances are currently being confirmed. items._cn_summary: 意大利后朋克与暗潮乐队Christine Plays Viola在其2026年专辑《F.I.V.E.》发行六个月后，推出单曲《At Last, I Found You》作为该专辑叙事的最终补充。歌曲以叹息般的合成器开场，营造雨天刹车的氛围，随后低音与鼓组建立推进力，吉他钩子切入，形成兼具俱乐部节奏与心理重量的哥特摇滚。歌词以深夜驾车驶入虚无为核心意象，描述主人公在公路上寻找自我，试图与被遗弃的童年纯真重新相遇，将死亡冲动重新解读为心理修复的尝试。音乐录影带将这一危机视觉化为雨夜中的城市穿行，画面笼罩在紫红与电蓝的灯光下。整体延续专辑关于恐惧内化、情感扭曲的核心主题，作为单曲独立发行时不作为专辑重心出现，以保留原始情感弧线的完整性。
