items.body: Boy Harsher have announced Get Mean, their first new album since the 2022 film and soundtrack The Runner. Due September 18 via Atlantic Records, the twelve-track album follows Jae Matthews and Augustus Muller through the breakup of their romantic relationship, a period of familial loss and creative uncertainty, and the difficult decision to continue Boy Harsher together. Alongside the announcement, the duo have unveiled “Hard Beat,” a lean, driving darkwave track accompanied by a Boy Harsher-directed video about surveillance, deviance, desire, and trauma. Where June’s “Jeans” introduced their return through wiry new wave guitar and western detail, “Hard Beat” bears down on the machinery that first made Boy Harsher such a commanding presence in clubs: a catchy bass-synth figure, an unrelenting kick drum, and Matthews’ voice cutting through the track like cold air rushing through an open car window. One cannot help but hear a trace of Depeche Mode’s “Behind the Wheel” in its fusion of movement, erotic surrender, and mechanical repetition. Boy Harsher pushes that feeling toward a harder, more body-driven strain of darkwave, with the bass carrying the physical weight while Matthews slips between confession, invitation, and command. The highway becomes both an escape route and a place where control can abruptly change hands. Directed by Boy Harsher with cinematography from Owen Smith-Clark, the video draws from Helmut Newton’s 1995 “High and Mighty” feature and the sexually charged queer punk cinema of Gregg Araki. It opens inside a windowless room lined with yellowed tiles, where an old CRT television displays Angel Zinovieff seated in a wheelchair. The image soon cuts from the monitor to Zinovieff herself, dressed in black with one leg held inside an elaborate metal brace. Rods and clamps run along her fishnet-covered limb, turning an orthopedic device into something between medical apparatus, restraint, and severe fetishwear. The camera studies the brace in close-up before moving to the controls of a vintage Cadillac tearing along a nearly deserted highway at night. Metal joints, pedals, switches, leather gloves, and the car’s gear selector enter into a visual correspondence with the hardware fastened around Zinovieff’s leg. The human body and the automobile appear as related machines, each capable of movement while remaining subject to whoever controls its mechanisms. Inside the Cadillac, Cheeky Ma and Mo Stark play the two “freaky deviants” hurtling through the blue-black night. The driver smokes, laughs, paws at the dashboard, and turns a handheld MiniDV camcorder on the other occupants, its mounted light firing directly into their faces. At moments, the camcorder is raised with the casual recklessness of someone filming a party while driving; elsewhere, its bright eye takes on the invasive force of an interrogation lamp. Rings, lacquered nails, facial piercings, glossy fabric, and black leather crowd the frame as passing streetlights sweep across the interior. Jae Matthews occupies the backseat beneath a black funeral veil. Red and green light divide her face behind the netting as she sings directly toward the lens, sometimes alone and sometimes pressed close against another veiled figure. The mesh softens and fractures their features, lending the encounters an uneasy intimacy: a kiss, a threat, and an identification photograph can seem separated by only a few frames. Matthews remains a passenger, yet her fixed gaze and repeated appeals to “make it real” steadily pull the car’s disorder around her. The highway is continually fed back into the tiled room through the CRT monitor. At first, the television shows Zinovieff in her wheelchair; it later carries the empty road, faces from the Cadillac, and camcorder images stamped with a red recording indicator and apparent geographic coordinates. Those transfers make it increasingly difficult to determine who is watching whom. The people in the Cadillac document each other, the closed-circuit system observes the room, and the video finally points its cameras outward at the audience. Under choreography by performance artist Monica Mirabile of FLUCT, Zinovieff’s physical restraint develops into a violent, increasingly expansive dance. She folds at the waist, whips her hair, claws at her clothing, arches backward, and strikes the tiled walls with open palms. Her movements carry the strain of a body fighting both its enclosure and the device attached to it. The editing cuts these gestures against the Cadillac’s acceleration, collapsing stillness and speed into the same state of agitation. Blue highway footage, sickly green tiles, sudden red washes, and overexposed camcorder glare keep the two locations visually connected. As the song intensifies, the cuts become faster and the images less stable: veiled faces double against one another, the driver leans toward the camera with a feral grin, Zinovieff’s hair lashes across her face, and the road stretches ahead without revealing a destination. Near the end, the Cadillac is viewed from outside, with its occupants compressed behind the windshield and Matthews’ veiled face visible within the moving vehicle. The car continues through the darkness as though escape itself has become another form of confinement. The video also sharpens the track’s resemblance to Depeche Mode’s “Behind the Wheel.” Anton Corbijn’s film famously presents Dave Gahan with an injured leg and crutches before a woman assumes control of the journey. “Hard Beat” rearranges that imagery around Zinovieff’s brace, the vintage Cadillac, female control, and the unstable line between passenger and captive. Those shared elements—bodily injury, roadway travel, erotic power, and surrendered agency—make the connection unusually specific, while Boy Harsher drives the idea into a harder and more openly confrontational setting. The MiniDV camcorder establishes another suggestive post-punk reference. Its repeated appearance in “Hard Beat,” together with Nathaniel Jerome’s promotional portrait of Gus Muller pointing a camcorder directly at the viewer while Matthews stands behind him, immediately recalls the artwork and promotional campaign for New Order’s 2001 album Get Ready. Photographed by Jürgen Teller under Peter Saville’s art direction, that campaign similarly placed a handheld camera between its subject and audience. With Boy Harsher calling their album Get Mean, another clipped two-word imperative beginning with “Get,” the parallel feels likely intentional, even though the duo have not explicitly confirmed it. Here, New Order’s invitation to be prepared becomes Boy Harsher’s warning to toughen up. Watch the video for Hard Beat below: Get Mean began during a period when the continuation of Boy Harsher was far from assured. In early 2024, after years of international touring, increasingly ambitious collaborations, and projects that moved between music and film, Matthews and Muller ended their relationship. The separation followed personal turmoil, family loss, and a creative block that left the prospect of another album feeling remote. The situation confronted the pair with questions that reached beyond the ordinary mechanics of making another record: What happens when a band that’s been forged in intimacy, cloaked in the sonic textures of darkly swooning electronics, and dedicated to plumbing the complex and contradictory depths of romantic feeling falls apart? What’s left after grief takes everything? What does a breakup album look like for a band as singular as Boy Harsher? Writing resumed when Matthews took to the road, moving through West Texas, the Pacific Northwest, South Florida, and points between. That unsettled geography became part of the album itself. Described as Boy Harsher’s “road album,” Get Mean was recorded across eight locations in the United States, Mexico, and Italy, gathering cellphone voice notes, environmental fragments, and changing emotional states along the way. Matthews describes the album as: “what I had to give during the most extreme period of my life.” Across its twelve tracks, the familiar coldwave propulsion of Boy Harsher meets detuned pads, squelching synth leads, pedal-steel bends, New Romantic guitar, percussive jokes, and unadorned recordings captured on a phone. Those additions allow grief and exhaustion to coexist with flirtation, humor, and the possibility of beginning again. The record follows the collapse of one form of intimacy while testing whether another—the creative bond between Matthews and Muller—can survive it. Get Mean arrives September 18 via Atlantic Records. Pre-order and pre-save the album here. GET MEAN by Boy Harsher Matthews and Muller formed Boy Harsher in 2014 after meeting while studying film in Savannah. Their first EP, Lesser Man, began as a small cassette release before the track “Pain” spread widely online. The duo followed it with Yr Body Is Nothing in 2016, the Country Girl EP in 2017, and Careful in 2019. Their filmmaking background came fully into view with The Runner, the 2022 horror film and accompanying soundtrack that they wrote, produced, directed, and scored. Their cinematic work continues with The Lonely Woman, their forthcoming feature-length horror thriller starring Chloë Sevigny, FKA twigs, Sturgill Simpson, Will Oldham, and Jake Weary. Boy Harsher are directing the film and providing its score. Following the release of Get Mean, Boy Harsher will begin an extensive North American headline tour before continuing through Europe and the United Kingdom. The itinerary includes sold-out two-night runs in Chicago and Portland, a sold-out Los Angeles appearance at the Hollywood Palladium, and a London headline show at the Roundhouse. items.body: The Autumn Aurora have released “False Idols”, the Italian post-punk and darkwave band’s new single, out now on all major digital platforms through Volcano Records with an accompanying official music video. “False Idols” is the title track of the band’s forthcoming debut album, and follows the debut single “Plastic Altar,” released on June 26, 2026 through the same label. Volcano Records describes “False Idols” as tracing “the loneliness of those confronting a society dominated by propaganda, appearances and false models imposed by politics, religion and mass media,” portraying a reality in which the weakest are crushed rather than protected while false prophets serve the interests of those in power. That same loneliness, per the label, turns into clarity: stepping outside the media spectacle means rediscovering oneself and rejecting a world built on money, easy smiles and illusions. Musically, “False Idols” pushes The Autumn Aurora’s post-punk and darkwave sound to its limits. Synths and analogue orchestral pads intertwine with two electric basses: one builds the groove alongside the drums, while the other takes on a lead-guitar role, using chorus, flanger and delay to shape cold, spectral atmospheres. The label credits the track’s vocals to Saveria Maitilasso, described as “deep and theatrical” – a different name from the vocalist, Vera Perkins, credited on the band’s debut single “Plastic Altar” in June 2026; Side-Line has not been able to confirm whether this reflects a lineup change or a different billing for the same performer. The Autumn Aurora, from ‘Plastic Altar’ to ‘False Idols’ “False Idols” arrives as the second single from The Autumn Aurora, following “Plastic Altar”, which the band released as its debut single on June 26, 2026, also via Volcano Records and also backed by an official video. Both tracks are pulled from the band’s forthcoming debut album, also titled “False Idols.” About The Autumn Aurora The Autumn Aurora is a Rome-based post-punk and darkwave band built around a rare two-bass lineup, with no standard guitar, alongside keyboards and drums. Side-Line previously reported on the band’s debut single “Plastic Altar”, released June 26, 2026 through Volcano Records & Promotion, the Turin-based label, and credited at the time to a lineup of Vera Perkins (vocals), Stefano Ferramola (bass), Francesca Buompane (bass), Chiara Bellucco (drums) and Fabrizio “Nemo” Mancini (keyboards). “Plastic Altar” was recorded, mixed and mastered at GreenMountainAudio Studio with Danilo Silvestri. The band’s forthcoming debut album, “False Idols,” has previously been reported for a September 11, 2026 release on Volcano Records; the label’s new single of the same title is the second piece of music shared from that album. Further band information is available through the group’s Linktree.
items._cn_summary: 罗马乐队The Autumn Aurora发布第二支单曲《False Idols》，作为同名首张专辑的先行曲目。该作品以合成器与模拟管弦乐音色垫底，采用罕见的双贝斯编制——一把负责节奏律动，另一把以合唱、镶边与延迟效果替代传统吉他，构建冷冽而幽冥的音场氛围。主唱Saveria Maitilasso的声线被描述为低沉且具戏剧张力。歌词层面触及虚假偶像、媒体操控与社会孤独等主题，反思政治、宗教与大众传媒所制造的幻象。作品延续乐队从首支单曲《Plastic Altar》以来的暗黑后朋克美学，在传统四大件之外通过双贝斯拓宽音色边界，但整体仍属类型范畴内的常规探索，缺乏更进一步的实验性突破。

items.body: For an overview of the what, the why, and the where of this music, do read my review of Volume 1 of this series. Essentially, this collection is more of what made Volume 1 so infectious. Yet, what makes this music so fascinating in general, that is, beyond its unswerving ability to fill dance floors, is the fact that these two islands, part of the Paises Africanos de Lingua Oficial Portuguesa (PALOP) regions of the world, are the second smallest African country; Seychelles is smaller. There are only 12 villages on Sao Tom�, lots of rain forest and, not surprisingly, lots of rain. I mention this because one could be fooled into thinking, with music like what�s on offer here, there must have been a music scene larger than there actually was. Not that little was happening, but that less got recorded or released than it might have had there been a city such as Lagos or Nairobi with the studios, labels, and pressing plants to better document it all. The music here, like Volume 1- recorded during Africa�s so-called golden age- is known as Puxa, a complex stew of ingredients from other former African Portuguese colonies mixed with rhythms that, with the help of dancers, can summon spirits or exorcise demons. At least according to some. It�s worth knowing that a 100 years or so ago, the Portuguese banned Puxa dance; it�s also worth knowing they appear to have failed miserably at this silly endeavor. Tucked away in modern Puxa is merengue, Kompas, Soukouss, Benga, and much else. One suspects much of this is coincidental, while other grooves were definitely imported considering both Portuguese rule and the islands� location over the Atlantic from the Caribbean. But don�t be fooled into thinking these two islands don�t have their own thing, as the sounds on this collection show. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s - Pedro Lima Pedro Lima, who has featured in his own Bongo Joe collection, leads a fiery band, complete with choked guitar vamps tussling with a kit drummer as a lead guitar comments from the sidelines on �Sossegado.� Elsewhere, Sangazuza demonstrates what happens when the bass and keys drop out, leaving the drummers and guitars to ride out a groove and drive dancers mad in the process. Check �Sono s� ku� de t�ma� or �Mairo bi cedo� for their ability to place a firm finger on the pulse. Over 15 tracks, the collection shows off multiple guitars weaving and circling one another, with lead and harmony vocals constantly in response, becoming part of the songs� melodic framework. At any given moment, vocals give way as the music unspools and floats on grooves that must have gone on for hours live. Africa Negra�s �Apoi�mos a luta dos nossos irm�os� is one example. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s by Various Artists In general, what�s on offer here, like Volume 1, was recorded at Radio Sao Tom� e Principe (RSTP), often taped in the courtyard outside at night, and released on cassette or occasionally, vinyl. It captures the joy of post-1975 independence and only fizzled out as styles changed and musicians struggled to make ends meet. Yet, take a quick listen to recent RSTP programming, which features musicians such as Babilonia or Calema, and you�ll still hear Puxa rhythms, showing just how potent the music form this two-island nation is on a global level. And Bongo Joe, who have also released two volumes featuring the above mentioned Africa Negra, have given this music the treatment it deserves, with extensive notes on the country�s history, vintage photographs, and band discographies. Various Artists - L�ve L�ve (Volume1) (Review) Pedro Lima - Maguidala (Review) Ann O'aro - Bleu (Review)

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

items._cn_summary: Dominique Cravic与Les Primitifs du futur的第五张专辑延续了他们难以归类的创作路线——对78转速老唱片中遗存曲调的考古式打捞与重新激活。手风琴、萨克斯、班卓琴、尤克里里、特雷门琴、吹管与锯琴构成的乐器编排在民谣、法国香颂、拉格泰姆与杂耍音乐之间自由切换，既有1925年老歌的幽默改编，也有向法国抵抗运动传奇歌手Juliette Gréco致敬的严肃曲目。Cravic以近似法国老派歌手的口吻念唱，二十七首短曲呈现复古拼贴的态度。乐评将其与Dan Hicks的不可定义风格相提并论，强调这群七旬音乐家以严肃态度与充沛热情为被遗忘的风格注入新生命。整体具有世界音乐与复古跨界的趣味，但实验性与前卫色彩相对有限。

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是作曲家 David Dzubinski 为 Prism Quartet 创作的短篇作品《Two Views of a Prayer》，属于该四重奏发起的「Unlocking Your Inner Composer」协作系列。2025年11月在费城自由图书馆首演，邀来人声 Ursula Rucker、打击乐 Tyshawn Sorey 与小提琴 Carlos Santiago 三位不同领域的音乐人参与编配与演出。四重奏主体建立在当代古典与学院爵士的交界之上，旁支融入自由人声朗诵与即兴打击乐，使整首作品在不足四分钟内完成从粗粝到抒情的往复。Sorey 的加入暗示了即兴与实验维度，Rucker 的声音则提供文本叙事的可能。乐评本身更接近节目导语而非深度评论，仅提供演出场景与合作者名单，未展开音乐结构、作曲技法或音响特征的深入分析。

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?
items.label: Go' Danish Folk Music
items._cn_summary: 丹麦三人组合GuldGanger的首张数字EP收录五首作品，以传统北欧民谣为核心框架。主唱Mia Guldhammer的声音是专辑核心，开篇曲的粗犷小跑节奏为她的演唱提供了展示空间。口簧与风笛为原创曲目赋予推进感，扬琴加入为传统曲目提供精致底色，口簧与长笛、弦乐交织形成器乐作品的离调张力。整体氛围呈现古老而粗粝的气质，融合传统器乐与现代组合方式。五首曲目展现了一支已具成熟度的乐队，作为起点颇具潜力，但能否在完整专辑中保持深度仍待观察。

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."

items.body:
How do you celebrate 50 years of music by a band that blazed trails for the charged, hypnotic pizzica sound, breaking it out of its homeland in southern Italy? How do you look afresh at a sound that�s changed and broadened its appeal without ever abandoning its roots as a new generation took over the instruments? It�s a challenge, but what Canzionere Grecanico Salentino (CGS) have done is reframe some of the pieces from those earlier decades through the lens of those playing and singing the songs now.
The brainchild of Rina and Daniele Durante, early CGS avidly proudly staked out its territory as champions of an almost forgotten culture. In the hands of their son, fiddler/frame drummer and singer Mauro Durante, the original vision has gone global (he also has a successful duo with guitarist Justin Adams) and they�ve become a major name in world music for their energy and outstanding musicality. They�ve made people in so many countries believe in the pizzica. One big milestone acceptance came with working alongside the celebrated pianist Ludovico Einaudi on his
Taranta
project in 2014, which gave them an even wider reach and boosted them even high. Very aptly, a remix and remastering of the �Taranta� track with him is included.
In a world that loves to dance, this is dance music with depth and power that explodes out of the speakers. It honors the material from the past while keeping its eyes firmly fixed on the future, clasping hands across the generations to celebrate the band and its lauded history.
Il Mito
(The Myth) pays homage without ever being slavish. There�s a real, urgent energy to the music-making here.
The title cut was written by the older Durantes, a cornerstone of CGS�s early repertoire and a reflection on life in their part of Italy. Roberto Licci comes to sing with his son Emanuele. Early vocalist Rossella Pinto reprises her role on �Lu Rusciu De Lu Mare.� Yet this isn�t all hearkening to the past. The sounds have taken on new colors and arrangements as younger fingers play them. It�s still mostly acoustic, with a few electric touches like a synth bass to round out the sound.
This is still completely Italian music, the enveloping, dry sound of pizzica, something that�s evolved over the last half-century, moving from a regional to a global stage. The band, and their compositions, deserve the party, but it begs the question:
Where will all this be in another 50 years?

items.body: W�R, Kongero - Songbooks Live by Nordic Notes This collaboration between the five-piece Belgian instrumental group W�r, whose members specialize in bringing the music of earlier centuries to life, and Kongero, the acclaimed Swedish female acapella folk quartet, offers an unusual chance to explore how their two cultures, ostensibly so different, can come together. It might sounds an unlikely mix, but here�s a spoiler: it turns out they�re pretty much musical best friends. The album kicks off at a cracking pace with �Var �r Du?�, a bravura performance through a twisted, tortuous piece that manages to be both elegant and surprising. However, the true astonishment arrives at the end, when the audience applauds and you suddenly realize this was recorded live (actually over two separate performances). W�R, Kongero - Songbooks Live by Nordic Notes The musicians bring material from their separate traditions, plus one original, showcasing their skills in intricate, swinging arrangements for both instruments and voices. Thanks to their skill, the varied ideas fit together seamlessly so it�s brimming with delights, like the wonderfully-titled �Drinking Like A Sweet Swede,� where the singers layers their harmonies over a jaunty backing. Everything is intricate, performed with a glowing precision that can disarm the senses with its beauty. The highlight, perhaps, is the beautiful �Klosterjungfrun.� The slow, seductive opening draws in the listener, the voices airy and light, curling around each other as the instruments wind long their path their. It�s a beautiful piece, but really, just one gem among so many here. W�R, Kongero - Songbooks Live by Nordic Notes There�s never a foot wrong, no note out of place and the performances are passionate, stellar, a true collaboration of instruments and voices. Add to that a mix that�s sharp as a razor, and Songbooks Live is a truly outstanding album, a perfect illustration that people have more in common than separates them. And it illustrates exactly what artists can achieve live. With luck, they�ll work together again. Soon, please. Find the artists online. items.body: Echo by Emi Makabe L oss galvanizes, loss focuses, and musical artists turn loss into shared reflections. Emi Makabe has focused the passing of her father into a generous meditation on resilience and legacy with her second recording on Sunnyside Records, Echo . The title reminds us of the connections between generations. Here are ten musical memories that span time and culture, blending a modern jazz sensibility with a traditional Japanese soul. Born in Japan, where she studied Japanese traditional music, Emi Makabe moved to New York in 2008. She is an educator and contributor to the jazz scene, composing and performing her own music. Her previous recordings, an EP on the Japanese Jazz label D-Musica Out of Time (2016) and Anniversary (2020), laid the foundation of her sound: soaring, sweet singing in Japanese, English and wordless vocalizing, accompanied by her flute and shamisen on top of jazz-inspired piano, drums, and double bass. Using these materials, Makabe celebrates the legacy of her father, supported by Thomas Morgan (double bass, backing vocals) and Vitor Gon�alves (piano, accordion, Wurlitzer electric piano), both of whom return from her previous records, as well as Kenny Wollesen (drums, percussion, vibraphone, electronics). Also appearing as guests are Meshell Ndegeocello (spoken word), Jason Moran (piano), and Bill Frisell (acoustic guitar) on the opening track. Echo by Emi Makabe Opening with Frisell�s acoustic guitar and confidently sentimental, �Birthday Song� comes to grips with loss, featuring a touching spoken meditation and a haunting Frisell solo. It ends with the hope, �I wanna remember the warmth of being in your arms.� The record closes with �Overture,� anchored by Gon�alves� dripping Wurlitzer supporting Makabe�s Japanese exhortation, �Let's talk again, countless times/Let's talk, if we meet again.� Echo by Emi Makabe Besides the refreshingly unselfconscious sentimentality, Makabe strides confidently between the traditional Japanese melodies, instruments, and the language of her upbringing in her father�s world and the contemporary jazz of New York clubs. �Snow� begins with Makabe�s shamisen playing a pentatonic tune, while �Text� swings in a fast bebop, with Makabe�s flute and harmonized Japanese scat singing. Echo by Emi Makabe �Morisan� hurries between worlds led by bouncy accordion, rolling jazz traps, and a stylish piano solo by Jason Moran. Moran also shares production credits with Thomas Morgan and Makabe herself. Utterly unique in approach, and equipped with a lovely vocal instrument, and with a skilled and single-minded ensemble, Emi Makabe has created a passionate, introspective, and honest fusion of tradition and modernity to celebrate the passing of the generations. Find the artist online. Further listening: Carmen Souza - The Silver Messengers: A Tribute to Horace Silver Mamak Khadem - Rembrance Yussef Dayes - Black Classical Music

items.body: Ledio Cakaj relates how the “romantic longing” of Laïko sustained him as an undocumented Albanian teenager, living and working in Patras and Athens in the mid-90s Dimitris Mitropanos' 1978 album, Parapono Laïko (meaning ‘of the people’) is the popular music that has nursed Greek heartbreak since the middle of the 20th century. It grew out of rebetiko, the raw, syncopated music of Greeks displaced by the catastrophic population exchange with Turkey in the 1920s. The bouzouki, that pear-shaped long-necked lute, carried the music alongside its smaller cousin the baglama. By the 50s, composers like Vasilis Tsitsanis began pulling the genre toward the mainstream, and it emerged over the following decades into various strains: the heavy, lamenting style of Stelios Kazantzidis, the orchestral grandeur of... The post Low Culture Essay: Ledio Cakaj on Greek Laïko Music appeared first on The Quietus.
items._cn_summary: 本文聚焦希腊Laïko（人民音乐）流派的源流与文化语境，追溯其从20世纪中期由Rebetiko演化而来的脉络，提及Bouzouki等传统乐器的运用，以及Tsitsanis、Kazantzidis、Mitropanos等代表人物对主流化进程的推动。文章以作者作为90年代阿尔巴尼亚非法移民的个人经历为切入点，探讨Laïko音乐中浪漫思念的情感力量如何超越国界慰藉异乡人。这是一篇带有强烈文化与族裔视角的随笔式乐评，文本截断于历史脉络梳理阶段，未深入至具体声音分析或音乐评论层面。

items.body: The debut solo LP from Shovel Dance Collective’s Nick Granata is a whimsical triumph that weaves the humdrum minutiae of modern life into a rousing and transcendent progressive folk tapestry credit: Robin Bazalgette For traditional folk music, the Roud Folk Song Index looms large. Compiled by librarian and folklorist Steve Roud, the index catalogues more than 30,000 songs from the English oral tradition, making it one of the largest collections of its kind. Leafing through the index, the stories woven through the songs are as broad and varied as the collection is large. There are your predictable tales of war, death and love. But there are also countless other stories – about horniness, being broke and heavyweight boozing. Folk music at its core... The post The Goo Place: My Heart is Running Backwards! A Martial Artist! items._cn_summary: Nick Granata首张个人专辑延续其在Shovel Dance Collective时期的民谣探索，将日常生活的琐碎细节编织成一张渐进式民谣织锦。乐评引入Roud Folk Song Index作为讨论框架，指出英式口头传统中除了战争、死亡与爱情等典型主题外，还充斥着欲望、贫穷与豪饮等更贴近生活的叙事。专辑似乎延续了这一传统，以怪异而充满趣味的手法处理民谣素材，在传统民间叙事的根基上加入前卫实验色彩。整张作品被描述为一场精巧的胜利，既扎根于民俗传统，又试图超越其框架，向更高的音乐境界攀升。

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Panda Bear与Sonic Boom继《Reset》之后再度合作的产物，延续了两人对新迷幻美学的探索。乐评将其聆听体验比作透过万花筒观察世界——新旧音乐元素在其中折射重组，形成对当下世界状态的折射与反思。Sonic Boom过往与Spacemen 3的关联以及Panda Bear在Animal Collective中的经历，为这张作品注入了深厚的迷幻根基。专辑试图用具有催眠效果的音乐，将清醒的观察与逃避主义结合，作为对苦痛的回应。整体方向偏向氛围化的实验流行，对熟悉新迷psych美学的听众而言是一次风格延续，而非大幅突破。

items._cn_summary: 这篇乐评聚焦于作曲家 Richard Barrett 的专辑《Booth》中收录的“elsewhen”作品。文中提出了一个新音乐领域的口头禅——“这是一种教你如何聆听的音乐”，暗示作品对听众聆听习惯提出了挑战，要求耐心与主动参与。评论从这一视角切入，探讨当代作曲如何在结构与听感之间建立新的关系。作者并未在所提供的片段中详细描述具体的声音技法或乐器配置，而是以聆听姿态的转变作为讨论核心，强调作品本身具有教学性的聆听框架。该评论属于 VAN Magazine 发表的深度乐评，篇幅有限但观点明确，适合对当代严肃音乐与实验作曲感兴趣的读者进一步阅读。

items._cn_summary: 本文聚焦澳大利亚ELISION Ensemble成立四十周年纪念专辑，呈现Daryl Buckley与Peter Neville两位核心成员的合作历程。他们在墨尔本大学维多利亚艺术学院相识，长期共同致力于当代古典音乐领域的复杂节奏记谱与演奏实践，尤其以对连音符群的精准处理闻名。文章以对话形式展开，揭示了这支室内乐团四十年来在新音乐创作与诠释方面的默契与坚持。作为南半球重要的当代音乐团体，ELISION Ensemble的成员以学者兼演奏家的身份活跃于国际舞台，曲目涵盖大量委托作品与首演。该纪念专辑既是对乐团历史的回顾，也是对其持续推动当代音乐边界的肯定。

items.body: Review by Heart of the Matter — This fantastic concert, advertised as the "solo albums tour" in order to capitalize the expectatives originated in their 1975 sabatical, dedicated by each band member to their own project, remained until its 50th anniversary as a legendary, sought-after bootleg. Now officially released, it presents us with a Yes formation, including Patrick Moraz on keyboards (Wakeman's replacement), shining in the full splendour of their mid-seventies. Bold, exploratory and going full throttle from the start, the band is up to the energy level displayed in their previous studio release, the album Relayer. This is well represented here, of course, by Sound Chaser and the side-long epic The Gates of Delirium. Also, the same virtuosism and powerful sonic brilliance are put into the staple versions, such as Siberian Kathru and I've Seen All Good People, and an extraordinary rendition of Ritual, sending sparks from the bottom of those Topographic Oceans.The songs coming from the solo albums, in the form of excerpts taken from Jon Anderson's Olias Of Sunhillow and Moraz' Story Of I, offer a welcome relaxing moment, including also a newly fashioned, acoustic rendition of Long Distance Runaround, so brief as full of charm.What else? Oh, yeah, all this comes from the hearts and hands of musicians listening to each other tight, instead of to a metrognome. Rather to seize than to miss, don't you think?
items._genre: symphonic prog / progressive rock / live album
items._cn_summary: 这是Yes乐队1976年在罗斯福体育场演出的官方发行版本，曾以传奇bootleg形式流传五十年。乐队阵容包括键盘手Patrick Moraz，整体演奏充满力量与探索精神，与前一张录音室专辑《Relayer》的能量水平相当。现场演绎了《Sound Chaser》与长篇史诗《The Gates of Delirium》，另有《Siberian Khatru》《I've Seen All Good People》等经典曲目，以及一段来自《Topographic Oceans》中《Ritual》的精彩呈现。Jon Anderson的《Olias of Sunhillow》与Moraz的《Story of I》片段为演出提供了呼吸空间，还包含一段简短而充满魅力的原声版《Long Distance Runaround》。整张专辑展现了乐手之间紧密的互动聆听，而非机械节拍器的跟随。

items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — Released in 2003 on Music for Nations, 'A Natural Disaster' is the seventh studio album fromAnathema, and the first one written almost entirely by guitarist Daniel Cavanagh. Undeniably adarker offering, this album has always been the odd one out - neither a continuation of the band'ssmoldering death-doom early style, not a clear indicator of what future releases would sound like.Combining drab alternative rock tropes with atmospheric passages and acoustic interludes, 'A NaturalDisaster' is more of an attempt to redefine the purpose of the band. Sprinkled all over this albumare a myriad of great ideas, that are unfortunately way too scattered in the final mix, which makesthe album somewhat of a forgettable and unimpressive listen. The sorrowful music played on manytracks appearing here reminds me of Katatonia and Porcupine Tree, and more remotely of Paradise Lostand Riverside, which renders this particular Anathema album slightly derivative.Interestingly enough, featured on this album is Vincent Cavanagh's twin brother Jamie, who plays thebass guitar for the first time on a major release with the band, following his early departure fromthe original lineup of Anathema, sometime around 1990-91. And so, as an album I have been fairlycritical of, I have to say that there are fine moments that make up for the weaker parts. Suchinstances of inspired and original music include opener 'Harmonium' with its desperate tones andclaustrophobic atmosphere, the peculiar piece 'Balance', on which Vincent Cavangh sings through avocoder, creating a feel of coldness and distance that is backed up by the moody keyboards. The song'Pulled Under at 2000 Metres a Second' has a post-punk appeal and is one of the surprising entrieson 'A Natural Disaster', while the hauntingly serene title track sees female vocalist Lee Douglasproviding excellent guest vocals. The final 10-minute-long instrumental 'Violence' could have beenmore appropriately constructed in order to fit the aesthetics of the album, at least in my humbleopinion, while the rest of the songs don't do much for me. This album probably suffers from a lackof direction and coherence, but I understand that people find within it a sincere expression ofgrief and melancholy, which I am able to appreciate.
items._genre: post-metal / experimental / alternative rock / atmospheric rock
items._cn_summary: 这张2003年专辑是Anathema乐队的一次转折之作，几乎完全由吉他手Daniel Cavanagh撰写，标志着乐队从早期死亡厄运金属风格转向更具氛围感和另类摇滚色彩的探索。整张专辑融合了沉闷的另类摇滚元素、氛围段落和原声间奏，试图重新定义乐队方向。作品中散落着诸多出色创意，但最终混音中显得过于分散，导致听感缺乏连贯性和整体冲击力，部分段落被评价为略显衍生性。专辑中也不乏亮点：开场曲以绝望的色调和幽闭氛围引人入胜，'Balance'借助人声效果器和忧郁键盘营造出冷冽距离感，'Pulled Under at 2000 Metres a Second'展现出后朋克气质，标题曲中女声嘉宾的演绎宁静而动人。结尾的长篇器乐曲在结构上略显松散，未能完整体现专辑的美学逻辑。整体而言，这是一张承载真挚哀伤与忧郁情绪的作品，在方向感和一致性上存在不足，但仍有若干值得反复聆听的精彩段落。

items.body:
Strong new doublepack from Short Span’s increasingly prolific Natal Zaks aka Picture, following his excellent ‘Eeeeeeee’ label debut with a new set of driving, swinging specials, tipped FFO Convextion, Plastikman, Shinichi Atobe, Miles Demdike.

‘Uuuuuuuu’ follows suit from ‘Eeeeeeee’ with six distinctively brisk, detailed and aerated swingers ranging from crispy, tracky jack-tracks to friskier chord riders well poised for various points of the night. The mesmerising whisk of ‘Quuuuuuu’ sets up a dead strong suite taking in swingeing techno-house on ‘Ruuuuu’, and Brinkmann-meets-Grungerman hypnosis of ‘Miiiiiii’, whilst the frothing ‘Leeeeeee’ gets right under the skin like some Shinichi Atobe-meets-Convextion special for Chain Reaction, and the hardgroovers get served with friskiest shake of ‘Wooooooo’.

Yyyyyyyyy is also on the way, collect them all!
items._cn_summary: Picture（Natal Zaks）在小厂牌Short Span推出双张专辑《Uuuuuuuu》，延续《Eeeeeeee》的路线，收录六首节奏鲜明、细节丰富、通透感强的舞曲作品。风格涵盖脆爽的轨道式jack-track、灵动流畅的和弦推进作品，整体气质介于Convextion的氛围深度、Plastikman的极简主义、Shinichi Atobe的催眠质感与Miles Demdike Clift的空灵之间。'Quuuuuuu'以迷人的刷击质感开场，'Ruuuuu'呈现摇摆的techno-house一面，'Miiiiiii'融合Brinkmann的冷峻结构与Grungerman的催眠律动，'Leeeeeee'如Atobe与Convextion为Chain Reaction量身定制的作品般潜入听者皮肤之下，'Wooooooo'则提供更硬朗的groove选择。整体定位为舞池功能性与艺术性兼具的电子舞曲合集。

items.body:
Eglo co-founder & Rinse FM resident Alex Nut continues to come into his own as a producer with deep cuts of beatdown soul and broken beat sagely nodding in the direction of Dego, Waajeed, Theo Parrish.

Nut is feeling the funk three different ways on his 3rd solo EP issued in the past 12 months. His DJ-honed club instincts and feel for timeless soul feed forward into the lo-slung shimmy of ‘Bright’, glazing a Detroit-style house strut with harmonised and cut-up vocal motifs bathed in warmest keys, before lacing it with a skudgy acid line for later in the night on its ‘Re-FreQ’ mix. The heat keeps knees up, hips swivelling, on a classic Y2K West London broken beat flex mutual to his and Floating Points’ tastes, whereas ‘Duck Duck’ really dials it down to with a bed ways glyde in its velvet-clad bass and dreamily vapourised chords.
items._cn_summary: Alex Nut作为Eglo厂牌联合创始人和Rinse FM驻场DJ，在这张EP中以三种不同方式呈现funk律动。首曲将底特律风格的house骨架与切割人声和温暖的键盘和声融合，Re-FreQ混音版加入尖锐的acid音色以适应深夜时段。第二首展现了西伦敦broken beat的经典风格，节奏灵活动态。第三首'Duck Duck'则放缓节奏，以天鹅绒般的贝斯线与朦胧蒸腾的和弦营造出梦幻氛围。整张EP延续了制作人对深邃灵魂乐和broken beat的探索，致敬了Dego、Waajeed、Theo Parrish等前辈的审美方向，但整体仍属俱乐部舞曲范畴内的常规创作，实验性有限。

items.body:
Expanded double vinyl edition of Sex and Death, the 11th studio album by lauded Factory Records ensemble The Durutti Column.  Originally released in 1994 on CD, the album has now been re-mastered with 5 bonus tracks and appears on vinyl for the first time in a coloured vinyl edition.

"The writing and recording of Sex and Death closed an uncertain period for Vini Reilly and the group following the collapse of Factory Records in 1992. Factory founder Tony Wilson remained in post as manager of the band, but Sex and Death would be their last album with producer Stephen Street, famed for his work with Morrissey, The Smiths and Blur.

Writer and master guitarist Vini Reilly remained philosophical. “People say the Durutti Column is this or that. I don’t care, so long as we make good music. There’s screaming feedback on some tracks, heavy metal guitar, Spanish picking. It’s not just this ethereal trip. Don’t listen to the form, never listen to the form. Listen to the content.”

Stand-out tracks include Anthony (dedicated to Wilson), The Rest of My Life, and Believe In Me. Guest musicians include viola player John Metcalfe, vocalist Ruth-Ann Boyle (later to form hitmakers Olive with Tim Kellett), programmer Martin Jackson (Magazine, Swing Out Sister) and bassist Peter Hook, then on furlough from New Order post-Republic.

All 5 bonus tracks are previously unreleased, having been retrieved from a long-lost DAT tape located in Tony Wilson’s personal archive. All tracks on the album have been newly re-mastered in 2020 by Peter Beckmann and Technology Works."
items._genre: post-rock / ambient guitar / experimental pop / art rock
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑来自Factory Records厂牌旗下的The Durutti Column，是Vini Reilly在厂牌倒闭后的过渡期作品，由知名制作人Stephen Street操刀。吉他演奏为核心，融合西班牙式指弹、啸叫反馈与重型金属元素，打破乐队此前给人留下的飘渺氛围印象。专辑收录献给Tony Wilson的作品以及多首器乐小品，客座乐手阵容横跨新秩序的低音线、Olive乐队主唱的人声以及中提琴演奏，呈现出层次丰富的跨界编制。2020年重新母带处理后以彩胶形式首次发行黑胶，附带五首从Wilson私人档案中寻回的DAT未发表录音。整体风格介于氛围吉他、后摇滚与艺术流行之间，对追求前卫融合与厂牌历史的听众具有吸引力。

items.body:
Recombinant raver Low End Activist properly came into his own on this ’21 slice of inch-tight jungle saluting legendary inspirations from 4Hero to Photek, Source Direct, Digital and On Remand - and now newly pressed up to vinyl.

After minting the project in 2017 and cultivating grime mutations ft. Trim and Flowdan, Berlin’s Low End Activist more fully indulged passions for formative jungle touchstones on ‘Engineers Origin’ - the 1st plate under his eponymous label, part of a family with his prolific Sneaker Social Club. 

Entering a field of lockdown-spurred jungle emulators, LAE brought a real finesse to his sharply stylized mid ‘90s homages that elevates his work above the crowd. On the title tune he summons proper darkside spectres with poised balance of sci-fi atmosfear and technicality certain to keep toes off the ground, before ‘Look Up’ snaps into the tightest steppers motion with flinty drums and exquisite use of a screeching string sample from On Remand, and ‘Probability 1’ seals the deal with a sonorous subbass pressure cadged from Dead Prez, alloyed to depth-charged breaks.

Cold and deadly!
items._cn_summary: Low End Activist 2021年发行的《Engineers Origins》是一张向90年代中期jungle黄金时代致敬的回归之作，取材自4Hero、Photek、Source Direct、Digital等传奇制作人的影响。标题曲以精准的平衡调暗侧氛围与科幻音色张力，营造阴冷悬置的舞池压迫感；《Look Up》将紧密碎裂的鼓组与On Remand式的尖锐弦乐采样结合，呈现紧凑的steppers律动；《Probability 1》则借用Dead Prez的低频质感配合深水炸裂式的碎拍。整体定位是制作精良的复古jungle复刻作品，虽在同辈复刻潮流中展现出更高的技术细腻度与对原典的考据深度，但在风格创新和跨界突破方面相对有限，更多是对已有传统的精细化重制。

items.body:
Ostgut Ton’s freshest recruits trade in effortlessly rolling bleep techno and moodier meat motors primed to be played in the big house.

Along with the likes of Quelza and Inox Traxx, Berlin-based Justine Perry & Paula Kossi lend an injection of new blood to Berghain’s label revival. Their ‘Paired Works’ oscillate energies between Perry’s effervescent levity and Koski’s rolling momentum, with the latter at best on the stealth build of ‘Beyond the Line’ and finely poised, teasing pressure of ‘Opaline’, while Kossi best impresses with the concentrated, urgent canter of ‘Maeve’, with its plucky bassline, plus the dub chord-riding ‘Adnexa’, and Fadi Mohem-esque elegance of ‘Held in Place’.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由两位柏林新晋艺人合作发行，收录在Berghain旗下的厂牌。整体风格偏向俱乐部场景的电子舞曲，在循环的合成器节拍与暗色律动之间交替推进。Perry的作品以轻盈明亮的质感为特点，而Koski的作品则更具推进力与紧张感，其中《Beyond the Line》采用渐进式的暗流构建，《Opaline》则在悬置的压力中维持平衡；《Maeve》呈现紧凑急促的低音线条，《Adnexa》借助dub式的和弦行进营造层次，《Held in Place》则展现出近似优雅的精致感。作为厂牌新血的一部分，这张作品延续了柏林Techno的传统脉络，但更多聚焦于俱乐部实用功能而非实验性突破。

items.body: Guia Cortassa reports from Italy's Nextones, where stunning quarries, canyons, churches and mountain villages cause music and landscape to blend as one Photo by Martina Nicole Garbin At Nextones, every performance comes preceded by another composition: the one the landscape inscribes on the listener. Before a single note is heard, the body has already been reshaped by the walk, the altitude, the heat, the sound of the River Toce, and the fatigue of getting there. Now in its 13th edition, the festival unfolds over four days across quarries, canyons, churches, and mountain villages in Italy's Val d'Ossola, near the Swiss border. Not simply treating these sites as evocative backdrops, Nextones allows each of them to redefine the conditions of listening. Every venue... The post LIVE REPORT: Nextones 2026 appeared first on The Quietus.
items._cn_summary: 这是一篇来自意大利Val d'Ossola地区Nextones音乐节的现场报道，第十三届举办。音乐节为期四天，演出场地分布在采石场、峡谷、教堂和山村等地。乐评核心关注点在于场地与音乐的关系：每个演出空间不仅是视觉背景，而是重新定义聆听条件的元素。作者强调在音符响起之前，景观本身已在听众身体上完成了一次塑造——行走、海拔、气温、河水声、抵达的疲惫都成为感知的一部分。场地包括采石场、峡谷、河谷与高山村落，试图让音乐与地形融合。这种策划思路与场地特定音乐、环境音乐传统以及声音艺术实践相关，涉及地理声学体验。原文为节选片段，具体演出阵容和曲目信息有限，难以深入评价音乐本体。

items.body: “Talk about the blood.” Aja Monet says it again and again on “for the Congo,” and by the end you can’t unhear it. The blood is coltan, the metal torn out of the Congo to feed the phone in your hand and the car in your drive, and the war that keeps it coming. The AI boom is hungry for more, and the body count climbs to match. She calls the phones “the death machines in our palms,” and yes, she means the one you’re reading this on. The percussion is heavy and the ground keeps moving under her, and she rides it, picking up speed as the names stack up: Paul Kagame, cosy with the West, then the World Bank, the IMF, everyone with a hand in the till. She’s a surrealist blues poet by trade, but she’s said this one cuts too close to dress up, so she doesn’t. She lays it out and dares you to look away. The poem started at a march in the UK in 2024, when a woman beside her shouted about the blood on the phone in her hand. That shout became this. It’s the sixth track on the color of rain, her second album after 2023’s when the poems do what they do, made with Meshell Ndegeocello and Justin Brown, out 22 May on drink sum wtr. The video opens on Michel Kuka Mboladinga, the DR Congo supporter known as Lumumba Vea, and Monet has said his image brought her to tears. He spends entire matches standing frozen on a pedestal, one arm raised, dressed as Patrice Lumumba, the country’s first prime minister, murdered in 1961 by a firing squad with Belgian and CIA hands on it, then dismembered and dissolved in acid so there’d be no grave. Everyone around him sings and leaps; he holds still, a living statue keeping a dead man in the room. items.body: Review by siLLy puPPy — For its third act, PANCAKE underwent a complete makeover once again although band member andguitarist Walter Negele managed to at least retain one member with drummer Hans Derer stickingaround for the band's final release NO ILLUSIONS which came out in 1979. With a new cast ofkeyboardist Uli Frank, bassist Ralf Scheibe and female vocalist Biggi Zmierczak, the band droppedthe Gentle Giant meets Pink Floyd proclivities of "Out Of The Ashes" and focused more on a proggystyle of heavier rock not unlike early Frumpy or other similar German acts such as Night Sun,Message, Birth Control or Murphy's Blend. While the band's first two releases were rather lazy andchilled out, NO ILLUSIONS finally steps things up a bit without jettisoning some of the spacey Eloystyle keyboard effects.An even more forgotten album than the band's earlier offerings, NO ILLUSIONS suffers from much ofthe same lack of inspiration that the band has always faced no matter how many times Negele pickedup the pieces and tried to persevere through. An admirable mix of keyboard intensity woven intoheavier guitar riffs and soaring emotive guitar sweeps that are clearly inspired by Steve Hackettand the early neo-prog style. In some ways this version of PANCAKE sounds a bit like Anyone'sDaughter, the band which swapped drummers after the debut only PANCAKE lacks the same creative edge.The original album featured six tracks in the 40-minute range however newer release feature an equalplaying time of bonus tracks which includes unreleased material and live tracks.Once again this album was lumped into the Krautrock scene but honestly this band never really fitinto that sector of the German prog scene. NO ILLUSIONS is by far the most consistent album of theband's three album run but once again suffers from lackluster songwriting, rather aimlesscompositional developments and never really delivers the goods that take you where you really wantto go. It's the kind of album that teases and then drops the ball, the worst kind however once againnothing is overtly unlistenable. The melodies are pleasant enough and Zmierczak delivers a nicefemale fronted performance on the tracks which is a step up from the previous album. The Eloy-esquekeyboard tricks are also quite nicely incorporated into the rock mix but despite the flawlessintegration the overall compositional flow seems rather tame. Amazingly enough the track "Tears OfTime" reminds me of early Asia.It seemed that the album title signified that Negele was done riding the PANCAKE bandwagon and hadNO ILLUSIONS about spinning his wheels for another fruitless endeavor. Dripping with potential andlost opportunities, NO ILLUSIONS continues the trend of a band that just couldn't get over the humpto take things to the next level. It's admirable that PANCAKE managed to stick it out for a threealbum run when so many superior acts only managed to squeeze out a sole release however in this casethe band was starting to sound too commercial for the prog world and not accessible enough for thebooming new wave and AOR rock scene. It's an OK album but in the sea of excellence that dominatedthe 70s hardly an essential listening experience. Add to that yet another horrifying album cover andit was time to call it a day. I'm still waiting for a compilation titled "House of Pancakes" but sofar no such thing.
items._cn_summary: 这是德国乐队PANCAKE的第三张专辑，于1979年发行。乐队在保留吉他手Walter Negele的基础上更换了几乎全部成员，新加入女歌手Biggi Zmierczak。专辑风格从前作的影响转向更偏重的摇滚路线，键盘与吉他交织，带有早期德国前卫摇滚的特点，如Night Sun、Message等乐队的影子。键盘音色借鉴了Eloy的太空感，同时融合了Steve Hackett式的新前卫吉他风格。评论指出这张专辑是乐队三张作品中最为统一的一张，但仍然缺乏足够的创作灵感和突破性的作曲发展，整体旋律虽悦耳但趋于平淡，未能充分实现其潜力。女声演唱是相比前作的进步，键盘与摇滚元素的结合也相当流畅，但整体给人一种始终差临门一脚的感觉。

items.body: Review by BasMolly — This is an absolutely gorgeous album by this amazing band. If you enjoy listening to Peter Robinson (previously of Quatermass) exploring the outer limits of the Fender Piano and occasionally the ring modulator, then I recommend this album. Sadly however it is long out of print, in both its versions. The first issue is credited to Suntreader and the second release is credited to Morris Pert.Morris Pert drives this album along powerfully as the main percussionist and drummer. Although he is (was) an enormously talented painist too, here we only get percussion. This CD is in urgent need of a reissue. And if any other unreleased recordings by Suntreader should accidentally surface we need those too. At the time of writing this reviewer is aware of three Suntreader releases.1. The album Zin Zin on the Island label2. The album The Voyage under review here3. Side two of the album Luminos/Chromosphere by Morris Pert on the Chantry label
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由Sun Treader乐队录制，发行于2001年，是爵士摇滚与融合风格的代表作品。键盘手Peter Robinson（前Quatermass成员）作为核心人物，以Fender钢琴和环形调制器探索声音的边界，演奏极具实验色彩。打击乐手Morris Pert主导整张专辑的节奏架构，他在此仅以打击乐形式出现，放弃了钢琴演奏。专辑将电子音效处理与传统爵士乐器融合，营造出介于前卫摇滚与自由即兴之间的声响空间。乐评明确指出两个版本均已绝版，乐迷呼吁再版发行。目前已知乐队共留下三张录音，其中此作被评价为美学上极为出色的作品。整体呈现小众独立制作的气质，声音设计具有探索性，适合喜欢跨界融合的听众。

items.body: Colony 5 member and songwriter Magnus Kalnins releases the third album from his solo project Chaos Tamed, “Nordverk”, via I/O Music on July 24, 2026. The album mixes EBM, IDM and dark electro, described by I/O Music as the project’s “hardest and most concentrated statement yet.” “Nordverk” runs nine tracks: “Determination,” “Core,” “Nightmare,” “Advesaries,” “Destroyer,” “Slaughter,” “Conflict,” “Sodium” and “The Bells.” Track five, “Destroyer,” was issued in May 2026 as the album’s advance single ahead of the full release. The album is currently available as a digital pre-order on Bandcamp, with the “Destroyer” track streaming now and the complete album unlocking on release day; downloads are offered in MP3, FLAC and 24-bit/48kHz formats. No CD edition has been announced for “Nordverk” so far, unlike Chaos Tamed’s previous two albums, which both had physical releases. Nordverk by Chaos Tamed Chaos Tamed’s ‘Nordverk’ follows 2025’s ‘Elbrus’ Chaos Tamed previously spoke to Side-Line in an interview about the project, which Kalnins has described as more of a laboratory than a conventional band. That conversation followed the release of “Elbrus”, Chaos Tamed’s second album, issued via I/O Music on May 30, 2025 in both digital and CD formats. “Nordverk” is the project’s next full-length since then. About Chaos Tamed Chaos Tamed is the solo project of Magnus Kalnins, a long-standing member and songwriter of Swedish futurepop band Colony 5. The project began as a side venture during a creative hiatus from Colony 5 and has since grown into an independent body of work, moving between EBM, IDM, dark electro and futurepop, built on ethereal, ghostly vocals over pulsing basslines and cinematic textures. The debut Chaos Tamed album, “Shock Waves,” was released via I/O Music on November 9, 2023, and received a nomination for Electronic Album of the Year at the GAFFA Awards in early 2024. The second album, “Elbrus,” followed on I/O Music on May 30, 2025, available digitally and on CD. The advance single “Destroyer” arrived in May 2026, sharpening the project’s harder, more industrial edge ahead of the third album, “Nordverk,” out July 24, 2026 via I/O Music.
items._cn_summary: Chaos Tamed是瑞典futurepop乐队Colony 5成员Magnus Kalnins的个人计划，第三张专辑《Nordverk》延续了EBM、IDM与暗潮电子的融合路线，以幽灵般的人声叠加脉冲低音与电影感音景。厂牌将其定位为迄今最硬朗、最凝练的声明，先行单曲《Destroyer》于2026年5月发行，强化了更具工业感的棱角。专辑共九曲，仅提供数字格式下载（MP3、FLAC与24bit/48kHz），未公布CD版本。Kalnins将此项目视为实验场域而非传统乐队，2023年的首作曾获GAFFA Awards电子专辑提名。这篇文章本质为厂牌新闻通稿，缺乏对具体声音设计或作曲技法的实质性乐评内容，信息以发行信息与项目背景为主。

items.body: German dark EBM duo Prager Handgriff release the live album “live in Zwickau” on October 30, 2026 through emmobiz records. The label issues the recording as a vinyl LP set with a bonus 7-inch, and separately as a CD box. The album documents Prager Handgriff’s performance at the Elektrisch Festival, held at Club Seilerstraße in Zwickau, on February 28, 2026, in front of a sold-out club. Side-Line has covered the festival’s recent editions, including the 18th Elektrisch Festival and the 19th Elektrisch Festival line-ups. The vinyl set spans ten tracks across two sides: “Tibet,” “Arbeit,” “Schwermetall,” “Klaus” and “Für immer” on side A, and “Schindluder,” “Maschinensturm,” “Traumsequenz,” “Bilder” and “Frontal” on side B. It comes with a bonus 7-inch carrying a one-off live version of “Deutschland” featuring Calva Y Nada. The CD box edition presents the same eleven tracks in sequence, closing with “Deutschland” featuring Calva Y Nada. Order details for both the vinyl set and the CD box are listed on the emmobiz records shop. ‘live in Zwickau’ and Calva Y Nada’s Zwickau live series The pairing with Calva Y Nada on “live in Zwickau” continues a run of Zwickau live recordings on emmobiz records: the label also released Calva Y Nada’s own “El calor de Zwickau”, which likewise carries the joint “Deutschland” performance as bonus material. About Prager Handgriff Prager Handgriff is a German dark EBM project formed in 1990 in Witten by Stefan Schäfer (vocals, electronic drums) and Volker Rathmann (keyboards, programming). The duo used the name “Der Prager Handgriff” for its early work. Their debut album, “Arglistige Täuschung,” was released in April 1993, followed a year later by “Täterschaft & Teilnahme,” which helped establish the project within Germany’s electronic scene. Prager Handgriff released the album “Maschinensturm” via Infacted Recordings in 1995. In 2005 the band issued the best-of double CD “Handarbeiten” as a retrospective, again crediting itself as “Der Prager Handgriff.” The album “Arbeit, Sport und Spiel” followed on Electric Tremor Dessau in 2011, its first release of new material in several years. Prager Handgriff released “Das Letzte Gefecht” via Infacted Recordings in 2022. In 2025, “Arglistige Täuschung” was reissued on vinyl for the first time, on double coloured vinyl with three bonus tracks, through Assur Anshar Records and Rune Serpent Europa. Prager Handgriff’s February 2026 performance at the Elektrisch Festival in Zwickau is now documented on “live in Zwickau,” released via emmobiz records.
items._cn_summary: 德国暗黑EBM二人组Prager Handgriff于2026年2月在Zwickau的Club Seilerstraße举行的Elektrisch音乐节上完成了一场售罄演出，并以黑胶双LP加7寸单曲的形式发行现场专辑，CD盒装收录相同曲目。这张现场实录跨越黑胶AB两面共十首歌曲，包括《Tibet》《Arbeit》《Maschinensturm》等代表作，附录7寸则收录与Calva Y Nada合作的特别版《Deutschland》。两位成员——主唱兼电鼓Stefan Schäfer与键盘编程Volker Rathmann——自1990年成立以来持续活跃，此次通过小型独立厂牌emmobiz records呈现其音乐节的真实演出状态。文章本质上是唱片发行的信息公告，缺乏对音乐本身的深度评论与声音特征分析。

items.body: Kyiv-based dark rock and new age band AndrosLand has released a teaser for a new music video, “Душа Лісу” (“The Soul of the Forest”), set to premiere on August 8. The teaser is the band’s first music video activity since 2015. The video was filmed in wintertime Kharkiv, a regional center located roughly 20 kilometers from the border, and produced by the team of Cinemuse.films. Actors Anna Fedorenko and Glib Chaplin filmed the outdoor scenes barefoot in the snow during December 2025, with Chaplin appearing topless in the winter cold. AndrosLand founder Oleg Andros, who has served in the Armed Forces of Ukraine since February 24, 2022, thanked the pair for their “resilience in the name of art.” “Душа Лісу” introduces the Goddess of the Forest, a figure the band describes as bringing human souls into the world, remaining present throughout a person’s life, and guiding them into the afterlife after death. Andros described the song as “new age and rock with a solo on the bagpipe,” crediting bagpiper Anton “Kay” Korolyov for his performance. He added: “We’re waiting for the premiere with bated breath, because AndrosLand hasn’t released a music video in a long time – not since 2015. We put a lot of effort into both the song and the filming.” The track originated as an instrumental with a French title, “Je chanterai juste pour toi,” self-released on an EP in 2015 with French lyrics written by AndrosLand lead vocalist Marina Novikova in 2014-2015. The Ukrainian-language version, “Душа Лісу,” will feature on AndrosLand’s upcoming album, “Hope,” which does not yet have a confirmed release date. Angelina Nepokulchytska provides vocals on “Душа Лісу”; Oleg Andros wrote and composed the track and also performs on it. Vocals were recorded by Pavlo Tymchenko and Nata Sivkova, with guitar, arrangement, recording, mixing and mastering handled by Ivan Luzan at Soncesvit Studio. About AndrosLand AndrosLand was founded in Kyiv in 2011 by Oleg Andros and has released three albums. Side-Line previously covered the band’s EP “Ниточки карми” (“Threads of Karma”), released in March 2025. Andros has served in the Armed Forces of Ukraine since February 24, 2022, continuing the project’s output alongside his military service. AndrosLand’s new video, “Душа Лісу” (“The Soul of the Forest”), premieres August 8 and will accompany a track destined for the band’s upcoming album, “Hope.”
items._cn_summary: 乌克兰基辅乐队AndrosLand发布新单曲「Душа Лісу」（森林之魂）的音乐录影带预告，新歌融合了new age与摇滚，并加入风笛独奏段落，营造森林女神引导人类灵魂从生至死的意象。歌词以乌克兰语呈现，源自2015年一首法语器乐作品，经主唱Marina Novikova改编而来。MV在冬季哈尔科夫郊外实景拍摄，演员赤脚踩雪、冬季裸露上身等画面突显艺术牺牲精神。乐队创始人Oleg Andros自2022年俄乌冲突后一直在乌克兰武装部队服役，兼顾军事任务与音乐创作。新歌将收录于尚未确定发行日期的专辑「Hope」中，体现出战时背景下持续艺术表达的韧性。整体作品融合民俗叙事、宗教意象与实验性视觉表达，展现了东欧地下音乐场景在特殊历史时期的面貌。

items.body: Sheffield electronic pioneers Cabaret Voltaire are getting a remastered reissue of their eighth studio album, CODE, out 9 October on Mute. The 1987 record, long out of print, returns on limited edition “CODIFIED” marble vinyl and as a deluxe triple CD set, the latter adding two bonus discs of remastered period remixes plus previously unreleased mixes unearthed from the archive. The reissue launches today with Thank You America (John Robie Dub Mix), a remix by the influential producer, writer and musician that was originally earmarked as the third single from the original release. ‘CODE’ caught the band at their commercial peak CODE finds Richard H. Kirk and Stephen “Mal” Mallinder at the height of their commercial and creative powers, marking the point where the pair signed to EMI, opening the door to bigger budgets without any compromise on their vision. The album became Cabaret Voltaire’s most commercially successful, with two singles, Don’t Argue and Here To Go, both breaking the UK Official Singles Chart. Discussing the album’s political undertone in the new sleeve notes, Mallinder explained why CODE still resonates with the band’s own history: “This album captures a very interesting moment in time where we were moving into a technological world. Probably more than anything else Richard and I made together, CODE was a political record that we didn’t have to directly articulate as political, mostly because of what was going on in the background at that time.” CODE tapped into an increasingly uneasy relationship with technology, computers and programming that was creeping into all aspects of life, unpicking the codes of control to expose them, a preoccupation that would continue through the rest of Cabaret Voltaire’s work. The album features guest musicians saxophonist Simeon Lister, bassist Mark Brydon of Chakk and Bill Nelson of Be-Bop Deluxe. It was recorded at the band’s own Western Works studio in Sheffield, with Adrian Sherwood joining for pre-production before sessions moved to Red Bus Studios in London for mixing. The remaster comes from Denis Blackman, who has remastered every Cabaret Voltaire album for over two decades; work on this edition began back in 2019 with Kirk himself, before his death, and was completed using his notes in consultation with Mallinder and Kirk’s estate. About Cabaret Voltaire Cabaret Voltaire were formed in Sheffield in 1973 by Richard H. Kirk, Stephen Mallinder and Chris Watson, quickly becoming one of the founding acts of British electronic and industrial music. Watson departed in 1981, after which Kirk and Mallinder continued as a duo until 1994, before Kirk carried the name alone through a 2014 performance at Berlin’s Atonal festival. An interconnected run of releases, Shadow of Fear, BN9Drone and Dekadrone, followed in 2020 and 2021, shortly before Kirk’s death in autumn 2021. In 2025, Mallinder and Watson marked the 50th anniversary of the band’s first performance with a reunion tour, including an announced Roundhouse show. That run continues into 2026 with final US and UK dates tied to the live album ‘But What Time Is It Really?’, from which the pair also shared a live version of ‘Yashar’. The CODE reissue arrives alongside that renewed attention on the band’s catalogue, giving new and longtime listeners a way back into one of Cabaret Voltaire’s most pivotal records.
items._cn_summary: 本文并非原创乐评，而是关于Cabaret Voltaire第八张录音室专辑《CODE》重发版的新闻稿。1987年原版由EMI发行，时隔多年由Mute厂牌以"CODIFIED"大理石纹限量黑胶及三碟豪华套装形式重新发行，附赠多首重新混音及档案中挖掘的未发表混音。专辑录制于谢菲尔德的Western Works工作室，由Adrian Sherwood参与前期制作，伦敦Red Bus Studios完成混音。Stephen Mallinder在新的内页注释中谈到，专辑捕捉了技术逐渐渗透日常生活的特殊历史时刻，探讨了人与技术、编程之间日益紧张的关系，无需直接表述便承载了政治意涵。客座乐手包括Saxophone手Simeon Lister、Chakk贝斯手Mark Brydon及Be-Bop Deluxe的Bill Nelson。重制工作始于2019年，与已故成员Richard H. Kirk本人合作，由长期合作的Denis Blackman完成。

items.body: Dina Summer mix 80s italo disco, new wave, EBM and early 00s electroclash into a dark, retro-futuristic synth-pop sound, and the Berlin-based trio have released a new single, “Bats in Paris”, out now via Iptamenos Discos. The track arrived on July 15, 2026, and is taken from the band’s upcoming mini-album, “Children of the Night”. The song opens with a crisp synth intro that sets up Dina’s sultry, spoken-word vocal line, a delivery the band says evokes their earlier single “Girls Gang”, though this time pushed further into pop territory. Kalipo joins Dina on the chorus, adding a second voice to a track the band describes as a soundtrack “for stalking moodily through the night.” Bats in Paris by Dina Summer “Bats in Paris” also serves as the lead-up to the band’s next mini-album, “Children of the Night”, due out October 9, 2026, digitally and on vinyl through Iptamenos Discos, with a black vinyl edition and a blood red/black marbled vinyl edition planned. The nine-track record takes its title from Bela Lugosi’s line in the 1931 film “Dracula”: “Listen to them. Children of the night… what music they make.” According to the band, the title track turns up the intensity on their established dark disco sound, with high synths firing over propulsive basslines as Dina calls out to an audience of night creatures. Dina Summer will support the release with the Children of the Night Tour, which includes festival stops at Berghain, Wave Gotik Treffen, Amphi Festival, E-Tropolis Festival, Grauzone Festival, Out Of Line Weekender, Katzenclub Festival, Extramuralhas and Baroeg, followed by headline shows in Berlin, London, Paris, Athens, São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Santiago and Buenos Aires, among other cities. About Dina Summer Dina Summer is the Berlin-based collaborative project of Greek-German dark-disco duo Local Suicide and Bavarian producer Kalipo, who began working together in 2019. Their sound draws on 80s italo disco, new wave, EBM and early 00s electroclash, resulting in club-ready basslines paired with lyrics that range from dadaist wordplay to more direct, empowering themes. The band’s catalogue includes the single “Girls Gang”, released in 2024, and, in October of that year, the electro wave single “Schall & Rauch”, which followed the same run of dark, dancefloor-driven output. That trajectory continues with “Bats in Paris” and the announcement of the mini-album “Children of the Night”, due October 9, 2026.
items._genre: dark disco / EBM / synth-pop / italo disco
items._cn_summary: 这篇乐评介绍了柏林三人组Dina Summer的新单曲《Bats in Paris》及其即将发行的迷你专辑《Children of the Night》。该作品融合了80年代意大利迪斯科、新浪潮、EBM和早期电子克拉什元素，形成暗黑复古未来主义的合成器流行风格。歌曲以清脆的合成器前奏引入，搭配低吟的念白式人声，合唱部分由Kalipo加入形成双重声线。迷你专辑标题取自1931年电影《德古拉》中贝拉·卢戈西的经典台词，预告了一种针对夜间生物的暗黑舞池美学。乐队将通过欧洲及南美多座城市的巡演推广新作，包括Berghain、Wave Gotik Treffen等暗潮场景标志性场所。整体属于暗潮领域内偏流行的舞曲制作，舞池功能性较强，但实验性有限。

items.body: Lusine, the Seattle-based project of producer Jeff McIlwain, has released a new single called “Bird’s Eye” via Ghostly International. The track is the second single from his forthcoming album “Melting Days”, following lead single “Pendulum”, and mixes rhythm-driven ambient textures with warm, expansive synthesizer pads. “Melting Days” arrives digitally on August 21, 2026, with a vinyl edition following on September 18, 2026. Melting Days by Lusine “Bird’s Eye” moves at a deliberate pace, tracing a progression of pinwheeling bells across a melodic, rhythmic core. Where “Melting Days” as a whole explores memory, grief, transition and renewal, “Bird’s Eye” leans into the instinctual, drifting movement that has long marked Lusine’s approach to ambient composition. McIlwain wrote “Melting Days” during what he has described as a difficult and solitary period, and he assembled it more like a film than a set of individual songs, prioritising emotional flow over conventional song structure. Asked about that process, he explained: “I think this was a bit freeing for me, not needing to compromise on ideas.” Rather than a stylistic departure, “Melting Days” is being pitched as a return to the richly textured electronic terrain that first defined Lusine’s sound, recalling the spirit of his 2007 ambient album “Language Barrier”. “Bird’s Eye” is out everywhere now, with “Melting Days” following on Ghostly International. Lusine is also set to play Hidden Hall in Seattle, WA, on September 12, 2026. About Lusine Lusine is the recording name of Jeff McIlwain, an electronic musician and composer originally from Texas who has been based in Seattle for many years. McIlwain began releasing music in the late 1990s, initially as L’usine and later under the more minimal, ambient-leaning alias Lusine ICL for labels including Hymen. Under the Lusine name, he signed to Ghostly International in the mid-2000s, releasing “Serial Hodgepodge” (2004) and “Podgelism” (2007) before issuing “Language Barrier” (2007), an ambient album on Hymen that has since become one of the most cited records in his catalog and was singled out by fellow Ghostly artist Loraine James as a personal favorite. McIlwain went on to release a string of albums for Ghostly International, including “A Certain Distance” (2009), “The Waiting Room” (2013), “Sensorimotor” (2017) and “Long Light” (2023), alongside numerous EPs and remix projects. Beyond his own records, he has scored or co-scored several films with composer David Wingo, including “Snow Angels”, “The Sitter” and “Joe”. “Melting Days”, described in press materials as his tenth studio album, follows 2023’s “Long Light” and finds McIlwain returning to the immersive, textural ambient sound of his earlier work, with “Bird’s Eye” offering the latest window into that return.
items._cn_summary: Lusine（Jeff McIlwain 的西雅图项目）即将通过 Ghostly International 厂牌发行新专辑《Melting Days》，本文着重介绍了其中的第二首单曲《Bird's Eye》。该曲以节奏驱动的环境质感配合温暖开阔的合成器音垫，铃声旋律在节奏核心上方盘旋流动。整张专辑创作于McIlwain一段艰难而孤独的时期，主题围绕记忆、悲伤、过渡与更新，制作方式类似电影配乐，强调情感流而非传统歌曲结构，被定位为对其2007年氛围专辑《Language Barrier》风格的回归，而非风格上的转向。McIlwain自1990年代末开始发行音乐，作品横跨氛围、IDM与电子舞曲领域，并曾为多部电影配乐。专辑数字版定于2026年8月21日发行，黑胶版紧随其后于9月18日推出。
